description:
TITLE: Sources Sought – Design-Build (D-B) Services for the Automotive (United Auto Workers - UAW) Building E9 Roof Replacement, HVAC Replacement and Seismic Upgrades at the Clearfield Job Corps Center

 

 The US Department of Labor, Office of Job Corps Acquisition Services, has a requirement for a qualified firm to provide design/build services that include, but are not limited to, the complete design and construction for the replacement of the existing roofing system including the roof eaves, overhangs and the roof drainage systems, roof HVAC curbs, pipe penetrations, flashings, roof edge pieces, etc. as needed to provide a weathertight roof system. THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE. In accordance with Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) 10.001(b), this notice is issued for the purpose of conducting market research. Market research is being conducted to determine if there are potential small businesses with the capacity and experience to perform the required work. This Notice is not to be misconstrued as an Invitation for Bid or Request for Proposal.

 

 THERE IS NO SOLICITATION AT THIS TIME. This request for capability information does not constitute a request for proposals; submission of any information in response to this market survey is purely voluntary; the Government assumes no financial responsibility for any costs incurred.

 

 The full extent of the work will be described in the solicitation, which may follow at a later date. However, a summary of the services to be performed is provided as follows:

 

 The work includes design-build (design and construction) services for the complete design and construction for the phased replacement of the existing ballasted built-up roofing system with a new EPDM roofing system including roof eaves, overhangs, roof drainage systems, roof HVAC curbs, pipe penetrations, flashings, roof edge pieces, etc. as needed to provide a weathertight roof system for the Automotive (UAW) Building E9 which totals approximately 120,000 gross square feet (GSF). Also included is the design and construction of the replacement of roof mounted HVAC units and associated ductwork, replacement of roof mounted exhaust fans, and seismic upgrades to the building structure to bring it up to current seismic codes for Utah.

 The roof design shall meet current allowable wind loads for Clearfield, Utah. Work shall be in accordance with the National Roofing Contractors Association (NCRA) recommendations for the type of roofing system specified.

 

 The NAICS code for this project is 236220 with a size standard of $45 Million. The magnitude of construction for this project is more than $10 million .

 

 Firms interested in this requirement are requested to submit a statement of qualifications. Your statement of qualifications shall demonstrate the capacity of your firm to perform the services described above, and should include the following information:

 

 1. Provide two (2) project examples where the D/B Contractor has completed (substantially or final) the design and replacement of single-ply Ethylene Propylene Diene Monomer (EPDM) roofing systems within the last five (5) years.

 2. Provide two (2) project examples where the D/B Contractor has completed (substantially or final) the design and replacement of roof mounted HVAC units and associated ductwork and air devices within the last five (5) years.

 Project examples shall include the location of the project, the project owner, and a brief description of the services performed. Your synopsis should also include the date of contract award, the original and final date of contract completion. Using the previous project examples indicate the original contract price and final contract value.

description: Amendment to correct GEOGRAPHICAL AREA WHERE WORK IS TO BE PERFORMED: Pineville, LA.
sow_text:
DEPARTMENT OF VETERANS AFFAIRS

STATEMENT OF WORK (SOW)

Replacement of OR Package Chiller



1. INTRODUCTION

This Statement of Work (SOW) outlines the required work for the removal of an existing chiller and the turnkey installation of a new Trane Air-Cooled Scroll Packaged Chiller. This work will be performed at the Alexandria Veterans Affairs Health Care System Facility (AVAHCS) 2495 Shreveport HWY 71, Pineville, LA 71360

2. BACKGROUND

The current chiller unit has reached the end of its serviceable life and requires replacement to ensure continued, reliable chilled water service for critical HVAC and process cooling.

3. GENERAL REQUIREMENTS

Site Visit: Contractor shall perform a site visit prior to commencement of work to coordinate logistics, assess site conditions, and develop a project schedule to minimize impact to VA operations.

Hours of Work: All work shall be performed at 8:00 a.m. and 4:30 p.m. Monday through Friday as required by the VA facility, unless directed otherwise.

Contractor Qualifications: All personnel must have appropriate licensure/certifications and be properly trained in chiller installation, startup, and commissioning.

4. SCOPE OF WORK

The contractor shall provide all labor, equipment, materials, supervision, and transportation to:

4.1 Remove Existing Equipment

Disconnect all electrical, piping, and controls from existing chiller.

Provide and operate all necessary lifting equipment (e.g., crane) to remove the existing chiller unit from site.

Demolish and dispose of old chiller in accordance with federal, state, and local regulations.

4.2 Supply and Installation of New Chiller

Contractor shall supply and install one (1) new 120-ton Trane Air-Cooled Chiller (model CGAM120) as specified. The installation shall comply with manufacturer requirements and local building codes.

Deliverable: Delivery receipt of new chiller and installation completion report.

Piping Insulation

Description: Contractor shall install insulation on all new and modified chilled water piping connected to the new chiller, meeting industry standards for thermal efficiency and safety.

Deliverable: Inspection report confirming proper insulation of piping.

Recharging Glycol

Description: Contractor shall supply and install glycol in the chilled water loop per factory recommendations, ensuring system is filled to proper levels and concentrations.

Deliverable: Certificate stating glycol type, amount installed, and conformance with manufacturer guidelines.

Electrical Reconnection

Description: Contractor shall re-connect the new chiller unit to the existing electrical infrastructure, ensuring all connections comply with code and manufacturer specifications.

Deliverable: Electrical connection completion certificate and compliance checklist.

Startup and Operational Confirmation

Description: Contractor shall perform startup procedures and confirm the operational status of the new chiller, including checking for leaks, verifying controls, and ensuring the system operates as intended.

Deliverable: Startup report and operational verification checklist with customer sign-off.

Condenser Coil Specification

Description: Contractor shall ensure the new chiller is equipped with standard finned condenser coils (not microchannel coils), as per customer requirements.

Deliverable: Manufacturer certification or sales order verifying condenser coil type.

Warranty Provision

Description: Contractor shall provide a full parts and labor warranty for one (1) year, and an extended five (5) year warranty for the compressor, in accordance with manufacturer terms.

Deliverable: Warranty certificates for unit and compressor, with clear terms and contact information.

4.3 Reconnection and Commissioning

Reconnect chilled water piping and insulate/re-insulate as required.

Reconnect electrical systems in accordance with National Electrical Code and VA specifications.

Provide and install any additional devices required for proper operation.

Refill the chilled water (CW) loop with appropriate glycol-water mixture per manufacturer’s recommendation.

Perform startup and commissioning in accordance with OEM and facility requirements.

Startup must be performed by authorized Trane Service to maintain warranty validity.

Provide operator training for VA staff on new equipment.

Provide all operation and maintenance manuals in both print and digital formats.

5. VA-SPECIFIC REQUIREMENTS

Warranty: All warranty terms specified must be registered with the manufacturer and VA upon project completion.

Safety & Infection Control: Contractor shall comply with all VA safety, infection control, and occupational health standards, including construction barriers/containment if work is in or near patient care areas.

Submittals: Contractor must submit product data, installation drawings, wiring diagrams, startup/commissioning documentation, and O&M manuals to VA COR for approval prior to final acceptance.

Commissioning: Provide written documentation that chiller has been commissioned per OEM requirements and is operating as specified.

Personnel: Contractor staff shall wear VA-issued identification while on site and check in/out per facility procedures.

Sensitive Data Notice: Any VA Sensitive Data encountered during this work shall be protected in accordance with VA Handbook 6500.

6. DELIVERABLES/TIMELINES

Due to lead times of equipment expect an administrative NTP for the submittal/ordering of the equipment.  Arrangements will be made for the formal NTP based on lead times.  

Pre-Installation Documentation: Within ten (10) business days of Notice to Proceed, submit schedule, safety plan, and product submittals.

Project Completion: All work, including commissioning and training, must be completed within 30 calendar days from Notice to Proceed.

Post-Installation Submittals: Within five (5) business days following completion, submit as-builts, warranty registration, and commission report.

7. COORDINATION/CONT

sow_text:
Specifications for a dilution refrigerator system
This dilution refrigerator system consists of a Gas Handling System Refrigerator
(hereafter referred to as GHS) and two identical He3/He4 dilution inserts.
Performance Characteristics
• 	Base temperature: 	≤ 30mK
• 	Cooling power: 	≥ 40 μW at 100mK
• 	Cool-down time: 	≤ 2 hours to base temperature beginning from the start of
condensing the mixture.
• 	Operational temperature range, control, and stability: 30mK ≤ T ≤ 1.5K with 5%
temperature control and stability over the entire range.
• 	Experimental space diameter approx. 28 mm
General Specifications
Operating Features
• 	The Seller shall supply a sliding seal at the top, so that the vertical position of the
Dilution Refrigerator (hereafter referred to as the “DR”) insert may be adjusted
without rotation with respect to a NW50 flange in the host system. We will provide
general dimensions of the host systems in the figures below for the purpose of the
quotations. These top loading host systems are 2 cryo-magnets, with bore of diameter
of 35mm and a liquid helium refrigerator with 45mm bore. The top flange of all these
hosts is an ISO NW50.
• 	Optimized ³He/ 4 He mixture designed to operate with an external dump. These two
DR inserts must be designed to operate, with the same performance characteristics as
listed above, not only with the provided GHS but also with our existing GHS. Our
existing GHSs have a mixture volume of 10.5 liters. 2.8 liters of this volume
corresponds to He 3 .
• 	Regarding whom provides the He 3
/He 4 mixture: Tests at the manufacturer facility to
be done with their own He 3 /He 4 mixture. DRs will be shipped with no mixture to
ORNL. ORNL will load its own He 3
/He 4 mixture when the system arrives onsite,
with same volume, and same ratio composition.
• 	One external liquid nitrogen cold trap with one dewar capable of hold times of at least
7 days.
• 	At a minimum, pressure gauges/transducers on the dump, insert inlet, insert outlet,
and pump outlet.
Control System Features
The Seller shall provide a complete control system capable of autonomous, local control
of the DR system.

-- 1 of 4 --

• 	A Lakeshore 372 AC Resistance Bridge controller shall be provided.
• 	16 channel Lakeshore scanner
• 	Auto-cool down and auto-run routines allow unattended operation. Automated
cooling capability and manual override option.
• 	Control system source code shall be provided by the seller to allow for interfacing
with our software controls. The local control system shall be capable of
communicating both control functions and data logging to a remote computer by
using a TCP/IP connection that exports the data.
Sensors
The Seller shall provide the following sensors.
• 	Installed thermometry (Fig 1: location of sensors) including:
 	Precision-calibrated RuO2 sensor on Mixing Chamber (hereafter referred to as
the “MC”) of measuring the temperature over the entire operational temperature
range (30mK to 300K) and with resolution (±1–3 mK at 50 mK; ±2–5 mK at
100mK; ±5–10 mK at 300 mK; ±10–20 mK at 1K; ±20–50 mK at 4.2 K).
 	For diagnostic use, temperature sensors at the Heat Exchange (HX), at the
1K/condensation stage coil and the STILL. One of these sensors needs to be
useful for appropriate diagnostics from 0.3K up to 300K across the whole range.
The Seller shall provide calibration curves for all temperature sensors.
Fig 1: Location of sensors
Wiring and Connectors
• 	In addition to the wiring necessary for the sensors referred to in Section “Sensors”, at
least an additional 12 twisted-pair wiring of manganin and/or CuNi clad NbTi shall be
provided down to the Mixing Chamber for subsequent consumer use. Ends shall be

-- 2 of 4 --

terminated by an appropriate connector. Mating connectors for these leads shall be
supplied (e.g. Micro-D connectors)
• 	Those connectors related to sensors and those related to heaters should be distinct as
should those related to the DR and those related to subsequent consumer installed
components.
• 	Wiring/connectors associated with sensors and wiring/connectors associated with heaters
shall be installed in such a way as to maximize electromagnetic isolation.
• 	The Seller shall provide a toolbox with extra connectors and spools of spare wire.
Warming Heaters
• 	Three resistive heaters shall be installed in the following locations:
 	Mixing chamber (two heaters for redundancy)
 	Still
• 	The heaters shall be chosen to satisfy the operational temperature range and stability
criterion.
Physical Characteristics
• 	Two interchangeable sealed inner vacuum cans (IVCs), relevant dimensions shown in
figure 2. Note the inner diameter at the IVC lower end of ID=28mm, for the system to fit
in our existing cryomagnets. Option to have a second pair of IVC vacuum cans with
larger sample space (ID=45mm) and shorter length, to fit in our helium cryostats. Option
to be priced separately.
• 	Insert probe flange ISO NW50 with sliding seal
• 	Lifting eyebolt on top of the insert probe
• 	Pressure gauges/transducers on the He3/He4 reservoir (dump), DR insert inlet, DR insert
outlet, and pump outlet at a minimum. Pressure measurements (dump, condensing, still
and pump outlet)
• 	The IVC’s shall be constructed of thin-walled (.010-.020)” aluminum in the neutron-
window region below the Mixing Chamber.
• 	Space below mixing chamber: 60 mm and other relevant dimensions to fit our existing
host equipment are shown in Figure 2.
• 	Lower portion of the Mixing Chamber shall be gold plated.
• 	Gas Handling system will be located (25-30) feet away from the insert. Try to mount all
components in one tower/cabinet not larger than dimensions shown in Figure 3.
• 	Gas handling system including dry pumps, pneumatic gas handling, PC. Important note:
Seller to provide control system source code.
• 	Hoses from the gas handling system to the insert shall be 30 feet (9.1m) long stainless-
steel flexible hose.
• 	Gas Handling System (GHS) tower to not exceed dimensions shown on Figure 3.

title: Enhanced Mobile Satellite Services (EMSS) Equipment, Provisioning and Customer Care Help Desk Support
description:
The United States Space Force (USSF) provides United States Government (USG) and other sponsored customers with satellite communication services through a dedicated, government-controlled gateway. The secure gateway communicates with the contracted commercial Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite constellation, and traffic processed through the secure gateway may be routed through secure government networks, public telephone networks, or other third-party networks. The program provides cradle-to-grave services and support to its customers, including baseline network airtime access, sale and provisioning of authorized devices, 24/7/365 dedicated help-desk support, enhanced Government capabilities such as encrypted communications, comprehensive operation and maintenance of the secure gateway, and other services.

 The objective of this possible follow-on effort is to deliver provisioning support and 24/7/365 dedicated help desk support to all authorized EMSS customers, including the Department of War (DoW), Federal Government, State and Local Government, approved foreign and allied governments, and other sponsored customers. The contractor may be required to provide EMSS Service Management services including Telecommunications Service Order (TSO) order management, warranty support, inventory management, supply chain functions, sub-contract management, provisioning activities, gateway liaison services, Return Material Authorization support, reporting, and program management.

 The scope includes provisioning, invoicing, record management, and customer care services for users who access the commercial satellite constellation through the secure gateway. Services include Telephony (Voice), Data Transmission (Circuit and Packet Switched), Short Burst Data messaging, Tactical Push-to-Talk voice and data, Paging and Alerting, Multicast Data Broadcasts, High-Speed Broadband services, Secure Voice, enhancements/evolutions of those services, and additional commercial services introduced during the period of performance and included under separately managed baseline access agreements.

 The Performance Work Statement (PES) contained in this posting is a secured attachment. To get access please submit a request through SAM.gov, including at a minimium POC name/contact information, vendor/entity name and CAGE code. Only vendors with Active SAM Registration will be considered for granted access and the Government reserves the right to deny access as it sees fit. These additional security measures are to comply with SF/SSC PA guidance.

PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT (PWS)
FOR
Dining Facility Services
26-MAY-2022
1.0 General:
1.1 Scope: The contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, tools, materials,
supervision, and quality control necessary, except as specified in Paragraph 3.0 as
Government Furnished, to perform Dining Facility Services, as defined in this PWS.
1.1.1 Objectives (a) Nutritional, safe, and appetizing meals in satisfactory quantities
within planned eating schedules. (b) Sanitary, clean, and pleasant dining environment.
1.2 Background: The contractor will be required to provide full food service for the
Regional Training Institute (RTI) trainees located on Camp Robinson, North Little Rock,
Arkansas. The requirements of this contract include menu planning, cooking, serving
and cleaning for the following meals: Breakfast, lunch and dinner to be served in the
dining facility, sack lunches for field exercises and To Go meals. The estimated
numbers of meals during each 12-month Period of Performance: 28,748 Breakfasts;
28,748 Lunches, 28,748 dinners (86,244 meals for each 12-month period of
performance). These meals shall resemble the portion, variety and quality expected at
established restaurants and TM 10-412.There will also be a need to provide bag type
meals as well. The contractor shall perform to the standards in this PWS. Authorized
diners are identified by two classifications: Subsistence in-Kind (SIK) and Non SIK. The
government will provide payment for SIK diners only under this contract. Non SIK diners
will pay for their own meals via cash or other means. NOTE: This is an estimate of
meals based on class loads per year, for 5 years and does not guarantee more, less, or
consistency. Class loads (student throughput) depends solely on congressional
budgeting and awarded class quotas from the National Guard Bureau.
1.3 Period of Performance (PoP): The Period of Performance shall be 1 Base Year of
12 months and four 12-month option years.
1.4 General Information:
1.4.1 Place and Performance of Services: The contractor shall provide services
between the hours of (Breakfast 6:30-8:00 a.m., Lunch 11:00 a.m.-12:30 p.m., Dinner
4:30-6:00 p.m), except on recognized US holidays or when the Government

mission of the BEP is to manufacture and produce United States currency.
The Annex Building was erected in 1937 and features a limestone façade, constructed
entirely of reinforced concrete. The Annex Building features a central corridor with five
wings that span from north to south along this line. The building is between 13th and 14th
Streets and C and D Streets in the southwest quadrant of Washington, DC.
The Main Building, constructed in 1914, features a neoclassical design with an exterior
of Indiana Limestone and granite. It is located between 14th and 15th Streets in the
Southwest quadrant of Washington, DC.

needs to be replaced with a new structural steel platform. The roof of the chiller / power
plant wing located between A-Wing and B-Wing of the Main Building, is deteriorating
and has cracks and leaks are present in multiple areas. As a result of this aging, water
intrusion through the roofing layers into the building interiors impacts the functionality of

D.C., Facility (DCF) is comprised of the Main Building and the Annex Building. The
mission of the BEP is to manufacture and produce United States currency.
The Annex Building was erected in 1937 and features a limestone façade, constructed
entirely of reinforced concrete. The Annex Building features a central corridor with five
wings that span from north to south along this line. The building is between 13th and 14th
Streets and C and D Streets in the southwest quadrant of Washington, DC.
The Main Building, constructed in 1914, features a neoclassical design with an exterior
of Indiana Limestone and granite. It is located between 14th and 15th Streets in the
Southwest quadrant of Washington, DC.
The existing structural steel platform has reached a corroded and rusted condition and
needs to be replaced with a new structural steel platform. The roof of the chiller / power
plant wing located between A-Wing and B-Wing of the Main Building, is deteriorating
and has cracks and leaks are present in multiple areas. As a result of this aging, water
intrusion through the roofing layers into the building interiors impacts the functionality of
the spaces below and causes damage and hazardous conditions. This roof replacement
shall be demolished and replaced as part of the Cooling Towers replacement project, and
is expected to be performed between the demolishing of the existing steel platform and
the construction of the new steel platform

This is a Notice of Intent, not a request for proposal. The National Institute of Health, Clinical Center (NIH-CC) intends to negotiate on an other than full and open competition basis with the following vendor: CDW Government.

 Acquisition Description:

 The NIH Clinical Center (CC) is a 234-bed federally funded, biomedical research hospital located on the NIH campus in Bethesda, Maryland. The Clinical Center is the delivery setting for all NIH intramural clinical research protocols. The hospital complex consists of two main facilities that are connected to each other by “bridges”. The original 14-story building is 2.5 million square feet and continues to house the clinical laboratories, imaging sciences, surgical suites, and several outpatient clinics. The new 870,000 square foot facility houses inpatient units and day hospitals. The Clinical Center accounts for about half of all NIH-funded clinical research beds in the United States and accommodates about 7,000 inpatient and 70,000 outpatient visits a year. Patients are admitted to the NIH Clinical Center from all over the world for the sole purpose of participating in a clinical research protocol.

Scope of Work

Privacy Screening Secure Parking Lot InstallationHouston Field Office



1.0 Scope and Intent

Houston Field Office requires a contractor to furnish all labor, supervision, materials, equipment, tools, fasteners, transportation, and incidentals necessary to provide and install black privacy screening at the Houston Field Office secure parking-lot perimeter fencing, entry/exit gates, and sallyport fencing.

The purpose of this requirement is to provide maximum visual screening for Government vehicles and assets located within the secure parking area.

2.0 Place of Performance

Houston Field Office126 Northpoint DriveHouston, TX 77060

Work is to be performed outdoors at the identified facility.

3.0 Requirements

3.1 General Requirements

The contractor shall:

Furnish and install new, commercial-grade, exterior privacy-screening material.

Provide black screening material that provides 100 percent visual blockage or an equivalent product that provides complete visual screening when viewed from outside the fence line.

Ensure the material is suitable for continuous outdoor use in Houston, Texas, climate, including normal exposure to sunlight, wind, rain, humidity, and temperature conditions.

Provide screening material with a minimum expected service life of five years under normal outdoor conditions. The contractor shall provide manufacturer product information or other documentation supporting this requirement.

Install the screening using industry-standard methods and hardware appropriate for the existing fence type. All straps, ties, fasteners, clips, tensioning devices, and other installation accessories shall be included.

Ensure the installation is neat, secure, properly tensioned, and free of loose edges, gaps, sagging, or sharp exposed materials.

Remove and properly dispose of all contractor-generated debris and leave the work area in a clean condition upon completion.

Coordinate work scheduling and site access with the Government point of contact.

No removal, replacement, or modification of existing fence fabric, fence panels, posts, rails, gates, access-control equipment, or other site features is authorized unless specifically approved in writing by the Contracting Officer.

3.2 Back Fence and Entry/Exit Gates

The contractor shall furnish and install privacy screening on the existing back perimeter fence and entry/exit gates as follows:

Quantity: Approximately 540 linear feet, including the entry and exit gates.

Height: 6 feet.

Material: Black, 100 percent visual-blockage privacy screening, or an approved equivalent.

Installation: Install screening from the bottom horizontal rail to the top horizontal rail of the existing fencing, as applicable.

Gate Operation: Screening installed on entry and exit gates shall not interfere with the safe, normal operation, opening, closing, latching, locking, or access-control function of the gates.

3.3 Sallyport Fence

The contractor shall furnish and install privacy screening on the existing sallyport chain-link fence as follows:

Quantity: Approximately 85 linear feet.

Height: 12 feet.

Material: Black, 100 percent visual-blockage privacy screening, or an approved equivalent.

Installation: Install screening to provide continuous visual coverage over the required fence area. Installation shall not interfere with existing fence integrity, gate operation, or site access.

3.4 Alternate Materials or Methods

Offerors may propose alternate materials or installation methods that meet or exceed all stated performance requirements. Any alternate proposal must include:

Product manufacturer and model or product description;

Product specifications and visual-blockage rating;

Documentation supporting a minimum five-year exterior service life;

Installation method;

Any differences from the stated requirement; and

Price and schedule impact, if any.

The Government is not obligated to accept alternate material or methods.

4.0 Contractor-Furnished Materials and Services

The contractor shall provide all materials and services necessary for complete performance, including:

Privacy-screening material;

Installation of hardware and accessories;

Labor, supervision, equipment, tools, and transportation;

Delivery, unloading, staging, and installation;

Cleanup and disposal of contractor-generated waste; and

Any required permits, licenses, or approvals necessary for contractor performance, unless otherwise specified by the Contracting Officer.

The contractor shall identify any anticipated site conditions, exclusions, assumptions, or Government-furnished support in its quotation.

5.0 Period of Performance

The period of performance is 30 days.

The contractor shall complete all work, including cleanup and correction of deficiencies, no later than November 30, 2026.

6.0 Inspection and Acceptance

The Government will inspect completed work for compliance with this Statement of Work. Acceptance will occur after the Government determines that:

Required areas are fully screened;

The installed product meets the required visual-blockage and durability requirements;

Installation is secure, neat, and complete;

Gates and access points operate normally; and

The work area has been cleaned and restored.

Any deficiencies identified by the Government shall be corrected by the contractor at no additional cost to the Government.

B.3 STATEMENT OF WORK

The contractor(s) shall provide services at the VA Palo Alto Healthcare System (VAPAHCS VAMC) Pathology and Laboratory Medicine Service for Clinical Laboratory Scientists (Medical Technologists). This is a new requirement for the VAPAHCS VAMC which is needed to augment staffing shortages for current and anticipated vacancies over the next five years.

The duties and responsibilities of the providers include, but are not limited to the following:



Medical Technologist



Perform a full range of automated and non-automated laboratory procedures in the areas of chemistry, urinalysis, hematology, serology, bacteriology, and immunohematology according to established protocols.

Evaluates the suitability of the specimen for analysis, requesting new specimen if determined to be unusable. Prepares specimens for analysis; ensuring that the physiologic states of the specimen properties are maintained.

Selects, performs, evaluates, and monitors the performance of test procedures using manual and /or instrumental techniques in accordance with established protocols. Recognizes and reacts to indicators of malfunction; locates and implements corrections.

Conducts quality control procedures on equipment, reagents, and products and maintains proper records for quality control reports.

Calibrate, standardizes, adjusts and maintains instruments on which trained. Verifies correct instrument operation using established procedures and quality control checks and monitoring. Identifies the cause of common problems and makes repairs.

Evaluates the validity of data in relation to the test system and accepted assay procedures; correlates quantitative data with patient data (i.e., history, medications) to verify results.

Performs additional tests to clarify or confirm abnormal patient results. Recognizes abnormal results that require immediate attention by the ordering provider and reports them directly.

Responsible for the generation of laboratory results from the work area into the laboratory computer system

Edit and verify results recorded into the computer system.

Stock and maintain specialized supplies used in the work area.

Accession and receive samples into VA laboratory information system package for in-house testing or sends out to reference laboratories.

Perform phlebotomy to obtain patient specimens for laboratory testing including blood cultures and compatibility samples on an as-needed basis.

title: TECHNOLOGY TRANSFER LICENSING OPPORTUNITY: Self-Cleaning Seals (Electrodynamic Dust Shield Technology) (KSC-TOPS-101)
description:
NASA’s Technology Transfer Program solicits inquiries from companies interested in obtaining license rights to commercialize, manufacture and market the following technology. License rights may be issued on an exclusive or nonexclusive basis and may include specific fields of use. NASA provides no funding in conjunction with these potential licenses. 

 THE TECHNOLOGY: 

 In space applications, seals for hatches, suit ports, airlocks, and docking systems for pressurized volumes such as habitats, rovers, and space suits must be kept clean. This is necessary to achieve the extremely low leak rates required to ensure that crews will have sufficient breathable air for extended missions on planetary surfaces. Dusty environments, such as those of the Moon and Mars, pose challenges because seals (elastomeric and otherwise) – as dust accumulates on them – will no longer perform as designed, substantially increasing leak rates. Similarly, terrestrial applications involving environments with high dust concentration and pressurized systems (e.g., mining, material handling) must maintain clean seals to ensure safety and uptime. Motivated by the hazard lunar regolith poses to seals – and thus to achieving a sustained lunar presence – researchers in the Electrostatics and Surface Physics Laboratory at NASA’s Kennedy Space Center (KSC) have developed seals that actively self-clean in a continuous or periodic manner. 

 To express interest in this licensing opportunity, please submit a license application through NASA’s Automated Technology Licensing Application System (ATLAS) by visiting https://technology.nasa.gov/patent/KSC-TOPS-101 

 If you have any questions, please e-mail NASA’s Technology Transfer Program at [email] with the title of this Technology Transfer Opportunity as listed in this SAM.gov notice and your preferred contact information. For more information about licensing other NASA-developed technologies, please visit the NASA Technology Transfer Portal at https://technology.nasa.gov/. 

 These responses are provided to members of NASA’s Technology Transfer Program for the purpose of promoting public awareness of NASA-developed technology products, and conducting preliminary market research to determine public interest in and potential for future licensing opportunities. No follow-on procurement is expected to result from responses to this Notice.

1.0 BACKGROUND
The Defense Health Agency (DHA) is acquiring professional, medical-grade linen rental and laundry
services to support the healthcare mission of the Naval Hospital Bremerton Branch Health Clinic Everett

2. Statement of Work



BACKGROUND.  

This requirement, driven by VA Central Office and The Joint Commission (TJC) on Patient Safety, mandates that dental and medical instruments are no longer permitted to soak in solution overnight. It is imperative that all instruments are returned to the Sterile Processing Service (SPS) for sterilization on the same day they are used. To comply with this mandate, it is necessary to arrange motorized vehicle runs between the VA Greater Los Angeles Healthcare System (VAGLAHS) West Los Angeles (WLA) Campus  and selected remotely located clinical facilities. These transport services will be scheduled from Monday through Friday, excluding holidays. 





SCOPE.  

Contract Staffing: The vendor must provide minimum of six (6) motor vehicle operators (truck driver, class c) with valid Class C Driver’s license issued by one of the fifty (50) States of the United States of America and 6 utility vans, Monday through Friday except holidays.



Vehicles: The vendor is required to provide their own vehicles, which must comply with Department of Transportation (DOT) regulations, Department of Health standards, and Veterans Health Administration (VHA) Directives 1116 pertaining to the transportation of reusable medical devices (RMD). Each vehicle must be equipped with a separate partition that distinctly segregates CLEAN RMD from CONTAMINATED RMD to prevent the mixing of contaminated instruments with sterile instruments. All vehicles must be insured.

Motor vehicle drivers are required to perform courier runs between the VA West Los Angeles (WLA) campus and to specified remote locations for the delivery and pickup of dental and medical instruments in spill-proof containers. Drivers will proceed to the ground floor of Building 500, specifically to the rear loading dock of the Sterile Processing Service (SPS), where instrument containers are to be picked up. existing CRAC unit, to include the associated pumps and existing dry cooler that is attached to MCE 1211.

Project will renovate the existing C Level utility space located at C Level of Building 1 which will provide environmentally safe, comfortable, and compliant conditions for maintenance staff.

Contractor shall completely prepare site for building operations, including demolition and removal of existing structures, and furnish labor and materials to perform work for VA Project 561-24-600 Upgrade Mechanical Systems-C Level as required by AE drawings and specifications, including but are not limited to:
Steam Header Replacement and Distribution

Architectural and Structural Modification to Condensate Pump Pit 
Modification to Supply & Exhaust Air and Repair of Outside Air Intakes
Hazardous Material Remediation and Insulation Repair
Mechanical Room Drainage Enhancement 
Improvement of Lighting and Electrical Panels

Refinish Surfaces, Removal of Brine Residue, Overall System Tagging/Identification and Systems Monitoring, Safety & Security.
The contractor shall also furnish all labor, materials, tool, and supervision necessary to perform work for VA Project 561-22-600 Upgrade Mechanical Systems C-Level, in accordance with AE drawings and specifications.

 The resulting contracts will be multiple-award Indefinite-Delivery, Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) construction contracts. Work will be authorized through individually issued task orders.

The anticipated aggregate ceiling is $3 billion over an eight-year ordering period. Individual construction requirements will be competed through task orders among eligible MACC awardees in accordance with the ordering procedures established in the resulting contracts. The solicitation and resulting contracts will include procedures for adding and removing awardees during that period (on/off ramp). The initial seed-project scope estimated construction magnitude, applicable evaluation factors, and proposal submission requirements will be provided in the solicitation.

 Work under the MACC will primarily consist of general construction and may include, but is not limited to, maintenance, repair, painting, alterations, architectural work, mechanical systems, electrical systems, plumbing, heating, ventilation and air-conditioning (HVAC), civil work, earthwork, fencing, structural work, steel fabrication and welding, roofing, building renovations, demolition, new building construction, sustainable construction, design-bid-build, and design-build projects.

 Individual task orders may include one or more construction disciplines and will vary in size, scope, and complexity. All work will be performed in accordance with the requirements, specifications, drawings, and other documents applicable to each individual task order.

 LOCATIONS OF WORK 

 The National Institutes of Health (NIH), Office of Research Facilities (ORF) is the steward of NIH facilities and is responsible for the planning, design, construction, acquisition, maintenance and operation of NIH owned facilities, which include campuses in:

 

 · Bethesda, Maryland,

 · Frederick, Maryland,

 · Poolesville, Maryland,

 · Research Triangle Park, North Carolina,

 · The Rocky Mountain Laboratories (RML) in Hamilton, Montana.

 NAICS CODE AND SMALL BUSINESS SIZE STANDARD

 This acquisition will be conducted using full and open competition with reserves for eligible small business concerns.

 Approximately four (4) unrestricted/full-and-open awards; and

 Approximately sixteen (16) awards under small business reserves.

PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT (PWS) 

Lenel OnGuard System Service & Upgrade





DESCRIPTION OF SERVICES/INTRODUCTION: The subject procurement is for establishing a comprehensive service contract for the Naval Surface Warfare Center, Carderock Division, Acoustic Research Detachment (NSWCCD ARD), Lenel OnGuard system with LenelS2 physical security solutions. The procurement shall include the enhancement of the existing security infrastructure through the upgrade of the ARD Lenel OnGuard system, identified by system number 149064. This upgrade involves transitioning from the current OnGuard platform to the more advanced OnGuard software package where segmentation can be implemented, limited to one room, representing a major step forward in access control and security management. All hardware installation necessary has been completed, this contract is for software and programming only. 



BACKGROUND: At NSWCCD ARD, located at 33964 N. Main Ave, Bayview, ID, the existing Lenel OnGuard security system does not have an active service agreement with any contractors. The current Lenel system utilizes certified access cards with personal identification numbers. The database has 64 readers with roughly 500+ cardholders in the system. Physical installation of all required components has been completed, only software upgrade and segmentation programming is required.



OBJECTIVE: The contractor shall provide the personnel, tools, and equipment to perform the following: 



Comprehensive service to integrate the NSWCCD ARD Lenel OnGuard system with LenelS2 physical security solutions.

Provide Lenel software licensing to upgrade the existing Lenel OnGuard system# 149064 from OnGuard 32ES (v7.6.382.52) to OnGuard Enterprise 8.3 Update 1 software package or latest manufacturer-supported version necessary to perform segmentation to a single room. 

Provide program database segmentation licensing to the system software of a specific area defined by the Government at time of installation. 

This segmentation licensing shall be programmed onto a computer in the space at ARD where administration of the system for that room will only be accessible through that computer in the room. No other computers shall be able to change or access the segmented area system for the computer that is located inside this room. This controller cannot span Segments within the software. All hardware necessary has already been installed and only requires the software upgrade and segmentation.

SPECIAL QUALIFICATIONS: Must be an authorized Lenel distributor/reseller. 



APPLICABLE DOCUMENTS: N/A



GOVERNMENT FURNISHED EQUIPMENT/PROPERTY/INFORMATION: N/A



DELIVERABLES: N/A



SECURITY REQUIREMENTS: UNCLASSIFIED

All contractors must be US Citizens and will be subject to a background check upon their arrival at the ARD.  No persons with a felony conviction that is less than (10) years old, a registered sex offender, or on a terrorist watch list will be allowed admittance to the base.  The background check will require that all vendors present an active passport, or a combination of a driver’s license and a birth certificate with the embossed state seal. nearing or exceeding their operational EOL threshold.
The objective of this procurement is to replace the program’s authorized 2018 Freightliner
tractor. Although the asset has not yet reached its standard operational end-of-life (EOL)
lifecycle threshold, the EBU Transportation program secured formal authorization for premature
replacement due to severe structural, operational, and safety liabilities.
Local Purchase Approval was granted for the previous replacement purchase due to our unique
requirement not being available through the mandated source of supply. The Local Purchase
saved the Government in overall costs and ensured the tractor was delivered in a ready-to-
operate configuration with no additional cost or time needed for modifications. Local Purchase
Approval was granted for this replacement purchase on 25 September 2026.
2.0 Scope of Work
2.1 The Contractor shall furnish and deliver one (1) new, commercial-grade, heavy-duty Class 8
replacement long-haul tractor configured with an integrated dual-sleeper cab and manual
transmission to support continuous, multi-driver over-the-road operations throughout the
Continental United States (CONUS). The tractor shall be engineered and equipped to operate
reliably across diverse geographic terrains and extreme climatic conditions while hauling
hazardous materials (HAZMAT) and/or classified assets. To minimize engine idle time, optimize
fuel efficiency, and ensure driver comfort and electrical auxiliary reliability during mandatory
rest periods, the vehicle shall come equipped with a fully integrated diesel-powered Auxiliary
Power Unit (APU) capable of providing autonomous heating, air conditioning, and continuous
secondary electrical power without requiring the primary engine to run. Vehicle acceptance is
also contingent upon the successful installation of brush guards. Prime contractors are authorized
to utilize subcontracted support to fulfill post sale modification requirements.
2.2 The vehicle must be fully compliant with all applicable federal, state, and local motor
vehicle safety and environmental standards at the time of delivery, including all Title 49 Code of
Federal Regulations (49 CFR) and Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration (FMCSA)
requirements governing commercial motor vehicles and hazardous materials transportation. In

department: HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES, DEPARTMENT OF

description:
The Contractor shall provide comprehensive, enterprise-wide lifecycle support for Electronic Security Systems (ESS) at Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) facilities nationwide. This includes the engineering, design, installation, integration, and commissioning of new systems; preventive and corrective maintenance; inspection, testing, and repair; system modernization and upgrades; system administration and configuration management; software and license support; and 24-hour emergency response.

 Covered systems include Physical Access Control Systems (PACS), Video Surveillance/Video Management Systems (VSS/VMS), Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS), duress alarms, intercoms, turnstiles, gate arms, elevator-control interfaces, and the associated network infrastructure supporting these systems — primarily built on the Lenel OnGuard and Milestone XProtect platforms.

 Services span routine, recurring operations and maintenance (priced firm-fixed-price) as well as supplemental, non-routine work such as installations, major component replacement, and modernization projects (priced firm-fixed-price or, when properly justified, time-and-materials). This market survey is being issued to assist the FAA in meeting ongoing requirements for miscellaneous mechanical construction services for: alteration, extension, conversion, and/or modernization of existing facilities.

 This also includes new construction if required. These services will be required for commercial, industrial, and utility type of facilities located at the Mike Monroney Aeronautical Center. Task orders will be placed against the contracts to fund projects throughout the year.

 Work requirements under these contracts can range from $2,000 - $1,000,000 each. It is estimated that $13.6 million in mechanical construction task orders will be issued over the course of the entire contract period to include option years.

 Requests for task order proposals for projects will be issued to all contract holders for the mechanical construction trade, and will be accompanied by a project description, construction drawings, and usually detailed specifications. Projects can be directly awarded by the Ordering Official if needed. Expedited competitive procedures, e.g., rapid turn-around times TAT)/completion dates, generally under 15 days will be detailed in the request for task order proposals.

1. DESCRIPTION OF SERVICES. The Contractor shall provide services non-personal
consisting of furnishing all labor, equipment, materials and related items, and performing all
operations necessary to clean hoods and duct systems as cited in this statement of work. This is
to include, but not limited to, such procedures as using a power jet washer, hand scraping, and
hand wiping. Hood and duct cleaning shall meet the requirements of National Fire Protection
Association NFPA 96, paragraph 12.6. This requirement is for Moody AFB GA and Grassy
Pond annex.
1.1. Specific Tasks. The following is a general outline of the primary features of the work to
be performed. This outline is intended only to establish the broad scope of the work and does
not in any way limit the responsibility of the Contractor who shall be required to perform all
operations necessary to meet the requirements as established in this SOW.
1.1.1. Clean all grease and residue accumulation off the hood and ducting systems. This
cleaning includes the metal hood section, ducting, vents, fans, louvers, filters, bates and exterior
walls, roofs, etc., where systems exhaust to the outside.
1.1.2. All surfaces of the hood, ducts and associated fans shall be cleaned to bare metal.
Contractors shall be required to disassemble the fan shrouds as necessary to clean the fan.
After cleaning and inspection, the fan shrouds shall be replaced as they were prior to being
disassembled.
1.1.3. The Contractor shall provide and install a temporary shroud, connected to the outside of
the hood, on all accessible sides, and shall extend to the floor. The shroud shall be taped to the
walls and hood surfaces during the cleaning operation. The shroud shall be installed so that it
minimizes the amount of debris and water, which could splash onto adjacent equipment and
walls. When the pressure washing and cleaning operation is complete, the shroud and tape
shall be removed and any tape residue, which may remain on the walls or hood surfaces, shall
be removed and cleaned.
1.1.4. The Contractor shall provide protection to cooking equipment from falling debris as
well as clean any debris having fallen on the floor, on the equipment or having splashed onto
any nearby equipment or walls. Prior to leaving the facility it shall be returned to the level of
cleanliness it was before work started.
1.1.5. At the start of the cleaning, electrical switches, detecting devices, and system components
shall be locked, pinned, protectively covered, and/or sealed to prevent accidental activation.
When cleaning procedures are completed, all system components having been pinned, sealed,
etc., shall be returned to an operable state. The Contractor shall be responsible for servicing the
fire suppression systems at no additional cost to the Government, in the event of a discharge

Standard turnaround is 48 to 72 hours for cleaning and five business days for alterations that need tailoring. The contractor performs the work at its own facility, provides laundry bags, and keeps a tracking record for each item.

 The Government intends to award one firm-fixed-price, indefinite-delivery, indefinite-quantity contract with unit prices and estimated quantities of about 6,025 items per year. The contract will have a base year starting December 4, 2026, four one-year options, and an optional six-month extension. The requirement is set aside for small business concerns under NAICS 812320, Drycleaning and Laundry Services (except Coin-Operated), with a size standard of $8 million. Award will go to the lowest-priced quote that is technically acceptable and has acceptable or neutral past performance.

description:
This acquisition is for three (3) Philips Cardiac Workstation 7000 units, compatible trolleys, and implementation services for patient care at the National Institutes of Health (NIH) Clinical Center (CC) Department of Clinical Research Informatics (DCRI).

 

 • Product Service Code: 6515 – Medical Instruments, Equipment, and Supplies

 • NAICS Code: 339112 – Surgical and Medical Instrument Manufacturing

 • Place of Performance: Bethesda, MD 20892 USA

 

 POTS: 27-000177

 

 Description: 

 

 This is a notice of intent, not a request for a quotation. A solicitation document will not be issued and quotations will not be requested.

 

 The National Institutes of Health (NIH) intends to award a fixed price purchase order to Philips North America, located at 222 Jacobs St, East Cambridge, MA, on a firm fixed price sole source award basis to provide three (3) Philips Cardiac Workstation 7000 units, compatible trolleys, and implementation services for patient care at the National Institutes of Health (NIH) Clinical Center (CC) Department of Clinical Research Informatics (DCRI).

 

 The Clinical Center’s requirement is driven by interoperability with its existing EKG-to-CRIS environment. The SOW states that the Philips model can be added to the existing CRIS interfaces, enabling electronic orders/results and an automated workflow in which authorized staff can review, annotate, and sign EKG reports online for automatic upload to CRIS. The SOW further states that this automation is intended to reduce errors, keep reports digital, improve availability, and improve patient safety.

 

 A different manufacturer’s product that requires development of an additional interface would not meet the requirement as presently defined because it would add interface development, validation, implementation, and operational risk outside the intended scope. Accordingly, the unique qualification is native/established compatibility with the existing Philips-to-CRIS interface and workflow, not merely the manufacturer’s trade name.

 

 This acquisition is being conducted using policies unique to the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 13 – Simplified Acquisition Procedures, Subpart 13.106-1(b)(1), For purchases not exceeding the simplified acquisition threshold (SAT), contracting officers may solicit from one source if the contracting officer determines that the circumstance of the contract action deem only one source reasonably available. Contracts awarded using FAR Part 13-Simplified Acquisition Procedures are exempt from the requirements of FAR Part 6-Competition Requirements.

 

 Interested parties may identify their interest and capabilities in response to this posting. The determination by the Government not to compete the proposed requirement based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government.

 

 Comments to this announcement, referencing this posting number, may be submitted to the NIH, Clinical Center, Office of Purchasing and Contracts, prior to the closing date specified in this announcement, to the attention of Kristin Nagashima, Contract Specialist via email to [email] by November 23rd, 2026 at 5pm EST.

title: Construction of Chilled Water Plant and Site Utility Upgrades at VA Medical Center in West Haven, CT
description: The scope of the chilled water plant replacement consists of the demolition of the existing chilled water plant (building 16a) and construction of a new multi-story chilled water plant to include chillers, cooling towers, pumps, and all associated mechanical and electrical equipment. Due to the close proximity of the existing fuel tank farm adjacent to the existing chilled water plant, a new fuel tank farm will need to be constructed as part of the project, which primarily serves the central boiler plant, requiring close coordination with the medical center and ongoing related projects.The scope of the site utility upgrades consists of the replacement and upgrade of the existing fire protection water main and the domestic water main from Campbell Avenue to Building 15. Site utility upgrades also include providing utility main loops of chilled water supply and return, steam supply, condensate return, domestic water supply, and fire protection water supply which will originate from the new chilled water plant and back-feed to Building 1. The work also includes the installation of redundant electrical feeder from the utility demarcation point to Building 19 and coordination with the local electrical utility provider to provide further electrical redundancy offsite as well. In addition, new water storage tanks will be constructed. This project involves civil/site, mechanical, electrical, plumbing, structural, geotechnical, and architectural disciplines. The project must also comply with the DVAs Physical Security Resiliency Design Requirements (PSRDM). It is expected that the chilled water plant will be constructed to meet USGBC LEED Silver certification. The work is located adjacent to and within an active Medical Center campus which will be operational at all times. Impact to on-going operations must be kept to a minimum and carefully coordinated with the Contracting Officer and VAMC staff. In addition, the work area is constrained due to the active medical center operations which will limit laydown and storage areas during construction.

title: FY27 VRO Janitorial
description:
Presolicitation Notice 

 The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Northwestern Division (NWD), Portland District intends to issue a commercial services solicitation, W9127N27QA009, for Janitorial Services at the Vancouver Resident Office (VRO) located 4480 SE Columbia Way, Vancouver, WA 98661.

 The Contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, tools, materials, vehicles, supervision, and other items and services necessary to perform Janitorial Services as defined in this Statement of Work at the USACE Vancouver Resident Office, 4480 SE Columbia Way, Vancouver, WA. The Contractor shall perform to the standards in the contract and comply with all local, state, and federal regulations during the services performed. No services are required on Federal holidays. Normal service days are five days a week, Monday through Friday.

 The attached draft PWS outlines the required work, and the final table shows the Square Footage of the required cleaning area. A site visit is not planned for this project. 

 The solicitation will be issued as a 100% Small Business set-aside. The North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) Code is 561720 - Janitorial Services and the applicable Small Business Size Standard, as established by the U.S. Small Business Administration, is $22M. The Product Service Code (PSC) is S201 - housekeeping- custodial janitorial

 In accordance with Revolutionary FAR Overhaul FAR 12.201-1(c)(2), the Government may solicit quotations directly from suppliers for this acquisition at or below the simplified acquisition threshold. Vendors that respond to this notice and provide a valid point of contact may be issued the solicitation directly via email. It is the vendor’s responsibility to notify the points of contact below of their interest in this requirement.

 If adequate competition is not received the RFQ will be posted to SAM.GOV

 Solicitation issue date is anticipated to be on or about: 18-Nov-2026

 Solicitation close date is anticipated to be on or about: 23-Nov-2026

 The resulting contract will be issued on a Firm-Fixed Price basis with a 12 Month period of performance expected.

 Contract award date is anticipated to be on or about: 30-Nov-2026

 CONTRACTING OFFICE CONTACT INFORMATION 

 Contract Specialist: Nathean Stoner

 Email: [email]

 Contracting Officer: Suzanne W. Hunt

 Email: [email]

PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT

JANITORIAL SERVICES VANCOUVER RESIDENT OFFICE

VANCOUVER, WA



Date: 28 October 2026

General Statement.

This is a non-personal services contract to provide janitorial services and services shall not be provided which are considered closely related to inherently governmental functions. The Contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, tools, materials, vehicles, supervision, and other items and services necessary to perform Janitorial Services as defined in this Statement of Work at the USACE Vancouver Resident Office, 4480 SE Columbia Way, Vancouver, WA. The Contractor shall perform to the standards in the contract and comply with all local, state, and federal regulations during the services performed. No services are required on Federal holidays. Normal service days are five days a week, Monday through Friday. The cleaning days may vary if agreed upon in advance; however, the office must be kept clean for business operations Monday-Friday and cleaned after 5:00 pm.

This contract is for a period of performance of 12 months.

Definitions. Throughout this contract terms are defined as follows:

Contracting Officer (KO): The Government employee who is authorized to enter into, administer, and/or terminate contracts and make related determinations and findings.



Contracting Officers Representative (COR): The Government employee who has been authorized in writing as the contracting officer’s representative, acting within the limits of their authority.

Quality Assurance Evaluator (QAE): The Government employees responsible for checking Contractor performance.

Contract Discrepancy Report (CDR): A written record of unsatisfactory performance by the Contractor as observed by the Quality Assurance Evaluator (QAE).

Vancouver Resident Office (VRO): The destination of where the contract is to take place.

Period of Performance



Base contract services will begin on December 1, 2026, and will end on November 30, 2027.



Services are NOT required on federal holidays. Daily services falling on Federal holidays shall not take place or be rescheduled. Services other than daily, if missed, and/or falling on Federal holidays shall be rescheduled and performed at a time approved by the COR.

Services are to be performed after 5:00 pm. Services are to be performed prior to each normal workday, Monday through Friday.

Government Will Furnish



The Government shall furnish without cost to the Contractor the normal amounts of utilities, except for telephone service, to be used only in connection with the performance of the work. The use of areas by the Contractor and the Contractor’s employees shall be limited to the storage of supplies, and some equipment, as space allows, as well as recycling and garbage cans.



Contractor’s employees shall NOT operate Government-owned transportation vehicles or other project equipment without prior and specific written authorization by Contracting Officer’s Representative.



Contractor Shall Furnish.



The Contractor shall furnish all materials and cleaning supplies to include, but not be limited to, the following:



Toilet paper

Paper towels and working paper towel dispensers in the bathroom and kitchen.

Cleaning agents

Germicidal disinfectants, (all disinfectants for sanitizing services)

Deodorizers

Waxes and sealers

Waste basket liners and trash can liners

Mops, dust mops, clean mop heads, and mop buckets

Brooms, scrub brushes, and scouring powders

Toilet bowl Cleaners

Window cleaner and rags

Antibacterial hand soap and working hand soap dispensers in the bathroom and kitchen.

Detergents



The Contractor shall furnish a local point of contact that has the authority to address deficiencies identified by the COR.



The Contractor shall furnish all labor and equipment necessary to perform the work required under these specifications. Equipment shall be industrial grade. Contractor shall provide equipment list (make, brand, and model) for approval prior to commencement of this contract. Any changes to the equipment list throughout the period of this contract shall be submitted to the COR.



All equipment shall have adequate bumpers and guards to prevent marking or scratching of fixtures, furnishings, or building surfaces.

All electrical equipment used by the Contractor or the Contractor’s employees shall meet all applicable safety requirements. This equipment should operate at full-rate performance levels using existing building circuits. It shall be the responsibility of the Contractor to prevent the operation, or attempted operation, of electrical equipment or combinations of equipment, which require powers exceeding the capacity of existing building circuits.



The Contractor shall ensure that all employees are capable of demonstrating adequate knowledge of chemicals, tools, equipment, and techniques necessary to competently perform the work.

Upon completion of this contract’s period of performance and prior to final payment being made, the Contractor shall immediately remove all equipment stored at the VRO, the Contractor and the Contractor’s employees shall vacate such building space within three (3) working days after the effective date of completion, shall restore the buildings and grounds to their original condition as existed when the Contractor initially occupied the space and return office keys to the COR within ten (10) days after the effective date of completion.

Performance Standards and Guideline Requirements

The Contractor shall maintain the building areas listed in Attachment A: Frequency Table for Vancouver Resident Office Janitorial Services. The Contractor shall provide sufficient supplies, materials, and equipment to adequately maintain the premises at an acceptable level of clean as outlined in this contract. description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, New York District is issuing an invitation for bid to award a Firm Fixed Price construction contract for the demolition of existing building, site Improvements and provide a turnkey modular office facility. The building and site infrastructure are required to have a minimum life expectancy of 10 to 15 years. OPTOMETRY SERVICES
STATEMENT OF WORK
Subject
The Federal Bureau of Prisons (BOP), Field Acquisition Office (FAO), in Grand Prairie, Texas,
intends to establish a Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA) against an existing Federal Supply
Schedule (FSS) Contract for the provision of one (1) Optometrist. The Optometrist will provide
services for incarcerated inmate population at the Federal Correctional Complex (FCC), located
in Pollock, Louisiana. General information regarding the Federal Bureau of Prisons (BOP)
facilities can be located at www.bop.gov.
Place of Performance
The Optometry services will be performed in the Health Service Department at FCC Pollock,
FCC Pollock
1000 Airbase Road,
Pollock, LA.
Schedule
Work will be performed between the hours of 7:30 am and 4:00 pm, Monday through Friday
(excluding Federal holidays), typically consisting of eight (8), one-hour sessions per day, with a
30-minute unpaid lunch period, if applicable. A session is defined as one (1) hour of work. The
facility’s needs will vary depending on workload, but the Contractor is anticipated to provide an
average of 40 sessions per week; Under no circumstances shall the Contractor exceed 40 sessions
per week. The Contractor shall provide services for up to 1880 sessions during the Base Year,
and up to 1880 sessions during each Performance Period thereafter. These sessions may be
adjusted to meet the changing needs of the institution. Any change in schedule or adjustments in
sessions will require prior approval by the Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR). A
monthly schedule will be agreed upon after award by mutual agreement of all parties.
Due to the nature of the correctional setting, delays in work performance may be expected. Such
delays may include but are not limited to inclement weather, electrical or mechanical problems,
or other security matters. When contract employees report to the institution but cannot perform
services due to such delays, the Contractor will be paid for one (1) session. Typically, any
remaining sessions for that day will be suspended, the Contractor will be free to leave, and the
Contractor will not be paid for remaining non-performed sessions. However, if the institution
requests that the Contractor remain at the institution for eventual performance, the Contractor
shall be paid for such sessions.
Supplies:
Due to security reasons, all supplies and equipment that the Contractor may use while at the
institution will be furnished by the institution. The institution will not provide clothing or boot
allowance for this contract.
Description of Duties

-- 1 of 4 --

OPTOMETRY SERVICES
STATEMENT OF WORK
The contractor shall be responsible for the following tasks.
1. Providing verification of credentials, proof of malpractice insurance and medical
indemnification insurance in the amount specified in the contract.
2. Evaluation of patients as referred by the medical staff.
3. Providing legible written reports on all patients evaluated, to include but not limited to:
• 	Eye exams as requested
• 	Diagnosis of eye conditions
• 	Removal of foreign objects from the eye
• 	Physical findings
• 	Tonometry exams
• 	Recommendations for treatment and follow-up care
• 	Prescribing corrective lenses/frames as appropriate
• 	Fitting of eye glasses and adjustment of frames
• 	Individualized adjustment of exam equipment as needed
• 	Contractor must complete a minimum of 15 and up to 20 scheduled exams per eight
session day
• 	Utilize the Bureau of Prisons’ Electronic Medical Record to document the eye exam
The contractor will not:
• 	Supervise BOP staff
• 	Participate in inmate accountability
• 	Requisition, sign for, or pick up supplies
• 	Formulate policies or procedures
• 	Attend recalls or staff functions
• 	Be a member of the Employees Club
Attire
The contractor is required to dress appropriately for the work environment. This includes
business attire or scrubs (black and blue scrub uniforms are approved). The attire worn shall also
be appropriate for the correctional environment in which the contract employee will be
performing. Jeans (of any color), low cut blowses, T-shirts, sandals (of any type), tank tops, and
sweatpants/shirts are not considered appropriate professional attire. FCC Pollock will not be
responsible for providing a uniform allowance.
Health Requirements
The contractor shall ensure that the Optometrist is free of infectious diseases. Any individual
performing as an Optometrist under this contract who subsequently develops a medical condition

which might reasonably be expected to place other workers, patients, or the public at risk shall be
immediately removed from activities requiring performance of invasive procedures and activities
which might reasonably be expected to place other workers, patients, or the public at risk. In any
such case, the contractor shall be responsible, at no additional cost to the institution, for securing

Education and Experience
The optometrist must have the ability to work with an AIC population from a variety of cultural,
regional, racial and ethnic backgrounds. Must have knowledge of routine office related duties
including working knowledge of computers, word processing programs and be able to type. The
optometrist must possess good organizational skills, good interpersonal relationship skills and be

accredited program and must possess 1 year of experience in Optometry. Additionally, the
optometrist shall hold a current professional license that permits him/her to practice the

Sakvarelidze National Center for Disease Control and Public Health (NCDC) at the Richard G. Lugar Center for Public Health Research in the Republic of Georgia. Statement of Work 

“Increase Emergency Power”

Project: 650-22-104



07/07/2026

Providence, Rhode Island VA Health Care System (650) 





B.1 INTRODUCTION

This requirement is for construction services to increase the capacity of the emergency power system for the main hospital at the Providence, Rhode Island VA Medical Center. (VAMC).



B.2 BACKGROUND / DESCRIPTION OF WORK:

The Providence, Rhode Island VAMC intends to procure construction services to increase the emergency power capacity for the main hospital building (building 1).



B.3 CONSTRUCTION DOCUMENTS:

Contractor shall furnish all labor, equipment, certifications, supervision, and materials necessary to perform all operations in connections with this order. Contractor shall perform work in strict accordance with the Contract plans and Specifications, and all other supporting documents for this contract to include, but not limited to the following documents:

Refer to Section D for list of attachments.



B.4 SPECIFIC REQUIREMENTS:

Add two (2) diesel generators with paralleling capability and the associated distribution equipment with the adequate capacity to accommodate future additions and renovations to the hospital. The new generators are to be located in the vicinity of parking lot 8, with the distribution and control equipment located in the mechanical room in the basement of Building 1.



Two (2) electrical duct banks, combined in a single trench, will be required from the new Control Building. The dual duct bank in the single trench will turn toward Building 1 A-Wing just south of the existing utility boxes concrete pad and then turn north. The duct banks will then split in order for the normal power to the electrical room to enter the southeastern side of E-Wing Building 1 and the new power to serve the new panels will enter the basement of A-Wing Building 1. An electrical conduit will be required from the new Emergency Generator Control Building to Building T18.



The construction shall conform to Department of Veterans Affairs design manuals and technical specifications, as well as all applicable codes. Construction work will be coordinated with other ongoing projects at the Providence, Rhode Island VAMC. It is expected that the following disciplines will be required for the construction of this project: civil, mechanical, electrical, architectural, fire protection, structural and plumbing.



B.5 CONFORMANCE STANDARDS:

All design and construction accomplished pursuant to this contract shall comply with the latest editions of established standards. Any exceptions must be approved in writing by the Contracting Officer prior to construction startup. 



Contractor/vendor shall obtain all data necessary to prepare construction documents required. The Contractor shall confirm all existing conditions and field verify any document provided by the VA. The Contractor is wholly responsible for both the accuracy and the level of completeness of the final product. Failure to verify information is not acceptable. Info, such as drawings and other documentation, provided to the contractor shall be used for reference only.



Where different specifications require different considerations for the same item of work, the more restrictive specification will have precedence and will be followed regardless of the specification publisher. 



All materials and workmanship shall comply with the codes and standards adopted by the VA. All work shall be done in a first-class manner according to the best trade practices and to the satisfaction of the COR and CO.



B.6 HOURS OF OPERATION:

Normal hours of operation are Monday through Friday from 7:00 AM to 4:30 PM EST. All work is expected to be performed generally during normal hours of coverage unless approved by the COR or his/her designee.



Work that disrupts hospital operations shall be coordinated and performed off hours. This includes utility shut down, work with excessive noise/vibrations, odors, dust, etc. Coordinate with the COR for approval. Off-hours work will be at no additional costs to the Government.



Before commencement of work, the Contractor shall confer with the COR and Contracting Office to agree on a sequence of procedures; means of access to premises and building. All work performed, to include delivery of materials and equipment, shall be made with minimal interference to Government operations and personnel.



Work performed outside the normal hours of coverage must be approved by the COR or his/her designee.



Observed Federal Holidays can be found here: https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/pay-leave/federal-holidays/#url=2023.



B.7 SECURITY, IDENTIFICATION, PARKING & VA REGULATIONS:

It is the responsibility of the Contractor to park in the appropriate designated parking areas.  Parking of privately-owned vehicles by contractor personnel is prohibited on the hospital campus and is only allowed at the Davis Park location off Chalkstone Avenue.  Parking in designated patient parking areas is strictly prohibited. Parking on grass is also prohibited. Parking for equipment necessary to perform the work will be authorized in advance of starting the project. Parking passes will be issued by the VA Police. Parking by contractors will be regulated in accordance with Providence VAMC Policy Memorandum 07B-3 entitled Registration of Privately Owned Vehicles. The VA will not invalidate, or make reimbursement, for parking violations of the Contractor under any conditions.



All contractor personnel shall obtain a short-term identification badge issued by the Project Manager. Such badge shall be worn by the individual and prominently displayed at all times while on VA property. No employee of the contractor shall enter the project site without a valid identification badge issued by the VA.
