description:
Tri-Annual Electrical Inspection IAW the Performance Work Statement. 

Total Small Business Set-Aside, Quotes are due on 11/20/2026 at 16:00 (4pm) PST.
sow_text:
Scope of Work: Specific Tasks and Services 

Electrical equipment (including, but not limited to switchgears, switchboards, distribution panels, motor control centers, and all related components) is inspected, tested, and either maintained, or calibrated. All work must be documented. The National Electrical Testing Association (NETA) provides guidance which is considered best practice for the maintenance of electrical equipment; these practices should be followed to the extent possible. The Contractor shall perform testing and preventive maintenance upon facility electrical components using the most current addition of the National Electrical Testing Association (NETA), Maintenance Testing Specifications. The Contractor is to perform the following tasks:



(a) Use lint-free rags to clean conductors, contact points between the circuit breakers and main buss bars, buss bars and interior of the electrical equipment. Use a vacuum cleaner to remove large debris; compressed air is not to be used for this purpose. Visually inspect for signs of overheating, misaligned contacts, damaged insulation, or lose lugs.



(b) Replace defective or missing panel screws, bolts, fastening devices and hardware with like. Replacement screws/fasteners shall be from the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) or equal. Self-tapping machine screws may be used if OEM screws or equal are not available or if existing screw opening(s) will no longer accept the OEM or equal fastener (COR must approve the use of self-tapping screws). The Contractor shall not mix screw head types and shall match OEM head type whenever possible. Replace / install knock out plugs and filler plates in junction boxes, motor control centers, panels and similar items.



 (c) Lubricate all moving parts with manufacturer’s approved lubricants. 



(d) Test and exercise circuit breakers located in switchgears, switchboard, and distribution panels to ensure operation under overload, and short circuit conditions.   NOTE: All molded case circuit breakers (including frames size 225 amps or less) must be tested to determine if contacts open and reclose when breaker is manually tripped and restored. All panels are to be tested including emergency panels. If no failures are encountered and the test is fully documented.  



(e) Test ground fault protection devices for proper function if they are installed in the Facility Electrical Power System. 



(f) Inspect and tighten ground connections. Test ground resistance for the entire facility grounding system. Any method of ground resistance must be considered acceptable if it can verify continuity and quantify the impedance to ground, to include but not limited to fall-of-potential, induced frequency, and clamp on testing. If initial tests indicate a problem or concern (e.g., ground resistance greater than 25 ohms), a more detailed test must be performed using fall-of-potential or 3-point test. Where installed, the lightning protection system must be inspected and tested for continuity to ground, ground resistance and certification in accordance with Underwriters Laboratory (UL) standard 96A. 



(g) Identify the hot spots in the electrical equipment by using infra-red thermal detecting equipment. Tighten problem connections to meet equipment manufacturers’ specifications using a torque wrench or other approved devices. Objective of this work is to detect any loose, broken or corroded connections in the electrical system. Problem connections shall be replaced with new connectors / hardware and or tightened with a torque wrench in accordance with the equipment manufacturer’s specifications. NOTE: IR Scanning will be classified as work on energized electrical equipment.

(h) Calibrate and maintain adjustable protective relays. 



(h) Test all control systems equipment for proper operation after maintenance is performed and before placing them back in normal service.



(i) Perform Arc-Flash calculations and labeling of panels, motor control centers, automatic transfer switches, breakers / disconnects.



(j) All breakers rated at 100 amps or over will be subjected to primary injection to test all aspects of the overload trip functions of the breaker.



(k) Contractor MUST provide secondary backup sources (generators, lights, spider boxes, cables) for areas of the hospital that cannot lose full power.  

- Some areas like 5W the ICU, will require a generator placed on campus and cables that connect to the unit

- The cables connect spider boxes and must have at least one spider box per every two rooms.  

- There must also be a spider box to support the nurses’ station as well (at least one).  

- Extension cords must be placed for each spider box too.  



(l) Contractor must provide generator power for the Boiler Plant. Boiler Plant has equipment that can’t lose power and must remain operational for a 12-hour shutdown.  



(m) Contractor should provide power support for CLC areas, if full power is lost to the area.  

(n) Contractor must provide circuit breaker panel hardware that should be replaced or installed on panels that are missing screws, covers for the dead front, and misc. parts needed for a safe electrical panel.  



(o) Contractor must create MOPs for every shutdown and VA must approve them before they can work.  



(p) The contractor should be aware and prepared to adjust as needed.  Facility needs and operations must be handled and planned.



(q) The contractor must return in the event of a massive impact to the facility (like forgetting to turn on a breaker, leaving something open, etc.

sub_tier: OFFICE OF THE ASSISTANT SECRETARY FOR FINANCIAL RESOURCES (ASFR)
description:
Request for Information: Federal Occupational Health (FOH) National Staffing Support Services

 

I. Introductory

This is a Request for Information (RFI). This is NOT a solicitation for proposals, proposal abstracts, or quotations. The purpose of this Request for Information is to obtain knowledge and information on potential vendor interest for project planning purposes.

 II. Project Description

A. Background:

FOH provides defined health services as well as consultation to Federal customer agencies exclusively through Interagency Agreements (IAAs). FOH is a leading provider of occupational health services (OHS) within the Federal Government, delivering services to numerous federal agencies and supporting a large federal workforce. Services are provided when FOH enters into agreements that are negotiated with federal departments and federal agencies’ national headquarters, and/or with 

their regional/local components for products ranging from a standard package of OHS program components to an array of services, including clinical services delivery, expert medical consultation tailored to a particular federal agency’s OHS needs, wellness and health promotion, behavioral health services as well as organizational development related issues. FOH maintains sole 

responsibility for consulting with its federal customer partners.

 The Vendor’s main responsibility is to provide Contractors who deliver FOH services as outlined in 

the Performance Work Statement (PWS). FOH defines OHS as the seamless coordination of comprehensive services using a data-driven approach to assist agencies in achieving a culture of health and high performance. FOH comprehensive 

services include:

Clinical Health Services (CHS) - Occupational medicine services, including urgent medical care, medical examination, employability consulting, and case review services that focus on assessing the medical ability of employees to perform their essential job duties safely, reducing lost workdays, and increasing employee productivity, as well as fitness for duty services that focus on the 

assessment of the ability of the employee to meet immediate job demands, increase employee productivity and improve employee performance.

Environmental Health and Safety Services (EHSS) - Services to ensure a safe working environment through site assessments, environmental health oversight of all FOH occupied spaces, emergency preparedness and emergency response.

Wellness and Health Promotion Services (WHPS) - Services to assist employees in achieving and maintaining good health so that they can sustain peak performance through fitness classes and wellness programs.

 

Behavioral Health Services (BHS) – Employee Assistance Program (EAP), Work/Life and other behavioral health services designed to promote emotional well-being and a healthy life balance through stress management, financial legal counseling and professional referral.

Operations and Management (O&M) – Services supporting FOH operations, management, and associated 

service areas. FOH services are designed to improve health outcomes and employee productivity, while reducing occupational health risks, absenteeism and overall employee health care costs. FOH’s mission is to be the occupational health provider of choice for the federal government.FOH staff plays a critical role in ensuring FOH maintains its status as the premier consultant 

provider of integrated OHS to federal agencies and their employees. By offering flexible, cost competitive solutions, FOH sets the standard for a culture of health and safety across the federal workforce. The Vendor is required to provide Contractor support for all occupational health services that FOH provides, including health promotion activities, data collection, and Agency/FOH initiatives requiring collaboration.

title: RF Roof Replacement Project
description:
The Princeton Plasmas Physics Laboratory is seeking a qualified contractor to replace roofing on two existing roofs. The (C40 RF Building & C41 CS Building) which are past their useful life requiring costly maintenance to upkeep. Severe water infiltration occurs regularly at failing joints, punctures, and flashing. Portions of existing metal coping have pulled away during storm events causing large sections of membrane to separate from the substrate. A catastrophic failure to one of these roofs would negatively impact the ability to conduct the top priority experimental operations in the Laboratory.

The Subcontractor shall provide all materials, labor, supervision, equipment, and expertise required to replace the noted roofs and specified components per the associated contractdesign documents. Construction scope includes the following:

SOLICITATION NOTICE 

 MULTIPLE-AWARD CONSTRUCTION CONTRACT (MACC) FOR GENERAL CONSTRUCTION SERVICES 

 Solicitation No. 75N99027R00002 

 The Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), National Institutes of Health (NIH), Office of Acquisition and Logistics Management (OALM), Construction, A&E, Facilities and Leasing Office (CAFLO), anticipates issuing a Request for Proposals (RFP) for a Multiple-Award Construction Contract (MACC) to support the ongoing construction, alteration, repair, and maintenance requirements of the NIH Office of Research Facilities (ORF).

 The resulting contracts will be multiple-award Indefinite-Delivery, Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) construction contracts. Work will be authorized through individually issued task orders.

 This acquisition is anticipated to be conducted using competitive negotiated procedures under FAR Part 15. The Government intends to award multiple IDIQ construction contracts under FAR Subpart 16.5. Individual task orders will generally be awarded on a firm-fixed-price basis. The anticipated aggregate ceiling is $3 billion over an eight-year ordering period. Individual construction requirements will be competed through task orders among eligible MACC awardees in accordance with the ordering procedures established in the resulting contracts. The solicitation and resulting contracts will include procedures for adding and removing awardees during that period (on/off ramp). The initial seed-project scope estimated construction magnitude, applicable evaluation factors, and proposal submission requirements will be provided in the solicitation.

 SCOPE OF WORK 

 Work under the MACC will primarily consist of general construction and may include, but is not limited to, maintenance, repair, painting, alterations, architectural work, mechanical systems, electrical systems, plumbing, heating, ventilation and air-conditioning (HVAC), civil work, earthwork, fencing, structural work, steel fabrication and welding, roofing, building renovations, demolition, new building construction, sustainable construction, design-bid-build, and design-build projects.

 Individual task orders may include one or more construction disciplines and will vary in size, scope, and complexity. All work will be performed in accordance with the requirements, specifications, drawings, and other documents applicable to each individual task order.

 LOCATIONS OF WORK 

 The National Institutes of Health (NIH), Office of Research Facilities (ORF) is the steward of NIH facilities and is responsible for the planning, design, construction, acquisition, maintenance and operation of NIH owned facilities, which include campuses in:

 

 · Bethesda, Maryland,

 · Frederick, Maryland,

 · Poolesville, Maryland,

 · Research Triangle Park, North Carolina,

 · The Rocky Mountain Laboratories (RML) in Hamilton, Montana.

 NAICS CODE AND SMALL BUSINESS SIZE STANDARD 

 The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this acquisition is 236220, Commercial and Institutional Building Construction.

 PSC Code: Y1JZ

 The corresponding small business size standard is $45 million.

 The NAICS code and small business size standard applicable to the initial seed project is also anticipated to be NAICS 236220 and $45 million, respectively.

 ACQUISITION STRATEGY AND ANTICIPATED AWARDS 

 This acquisition will be conducted using full and open competition with reserves for eligible small business concerns.

 NIH anticipates awarding up to twenty (20) IDIQ contracts, consisting of:

 
 Approximately four (4) unrestricted/full-and-open awards; and

 Approximately sixteen (16) awards under small business reserves.

 

 The small business reserves are anticipated to include eligible concerns in the following categories:

 
 Historically Underutilized Business Zone (HUBZone) Small Business;

 Women-Owned Small Business (WOSB);

 Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB); and

title: National Coast Guard Museum- Facility Maintenance Services
description:
The U.S. Coast Guard (USCG) is conducting market research to identify capable sources, including small businesses (such as 8(a), HUBZone, SDVOSB, and WOSB), to provide comprehensive 24/7 Facility Maintenance services for the newly constructed National Coast Guard Museum in New London, Connecticut.

 The selected contractor will be required to furnish all management, supervision, labor, equipment, and materials necessary to ensure safe, reliable, and compliant museum operations. The facility consists of an 84,000 sq. ft., six-story waterfront building situated on under 1 acre of grounds.

 Core requirements include, but are not limited to:

 
 HVAC & Environmental Controls: Continuous operation and maintenance of gas-fired condensing boilers, chillers, cooling towers, radiant flooring, and Building Automation Systems (BAS) to maintain strict gallery climate tolerances ( 68°F–72°F and 45%–55% Relative Humidity ).

 Electrical, Plumbing, & Life Safety: Operations and maintenance of power distribution panels, emergency generators, fuel systems, fire alarms, fire extinguishers (NFPA 10), and water sprinkler systems (NFPA 25).

 Vertical Transportation: Monthly servicing, emergency response, and annual certified load testing for four (4) elevators.

 Custodial Services: A hybrid staffing model providing APPA Level 1 ( Orderly Spotlessness ) cleaning standards in high-traffic public galleries and APPA Level 4 in back-of-house staff areas.

 Grounds, Hardscape, & Snow Removal: Year-round exterior upkeep, power washing, and 24/7 bare-pavement snow and ice control (utilizing hardscape-safe compounds) for walkways, terraces, and flat roofing.

title: Z2DA--666-27-102 Lightning Protection Update B71N
description: GENERAL: Introduction: An inspection for current code compliance of the lightning Protection System on Building 71N has been conducted and found the system needs upgrades and repairs to meet current NFPA 780 and UL96A standards. The Sheridan VA Medical Center needs the services of a qualified contractor to perform the needed lightning protection upgrades to the main hospital building 71N. Located on the Sheridan Wyoming Veterans Affairs Medical Center (VAMC) campus, at 1898 Fort Road, Sheridan, Wyoming 82801. Statement of Work: Specifics a. Existing Conditions The existing lightning protection system (LPS) for Building 71N was installed in 1989 during the building s original construction. Overall, the system remains in fair condition, though it requires repair because several air terminals have become detached from their adhesive bonds to the roof surface. Air terminals are present at all high points of the structure, and all roof-mounted equipment and appurtenances are properly grounded. A main grounding bus connects the communication systems and possibly the electrical distribution system to the primary service ground. The specific location where the grounding system bonds together the structural steel, electrical system, lightning protection components, and plumbing to create an equipotential ground could not be identified during the assessment. A continuous grounding loop encircles Buildings 9, 71, and 71N, with all roof air terminals and down conductors tied into this loop. Down conductors descend to the loop at the corners of each of these buildings. Each air terminal has at least two separate grounding paths, satisfying current code requirements. No Transient Voltage Surge Suppression (TVSS) devices were observed in the system. The lower 8 feet of the ground down conductors are encased in PVC electrical conduit for protection. New Construction Recent construction has added large equipment and a screen wall to the roof, which now obstructs and interferes with the original positioning of the existing air terminals. This new equipment sits higher than the existing lightning protection system components, rendering the current air terminals ineffective at intercepting and safely directing lightning strikes to ground. Project Requirements To bring the existing lightning protection system (LPS) into compliance the following corrections are needed: Install Transient Voltage Surge Suppression (TVSS) devices at the building s main service panel. Establish proper bonding by interconnecting all electrical systems, communication systems, piping, and structural steel at the service entrance to create an equipotential ground. Repair all roof air terminals that have detached or pulled away from their adhesive mounts on the roof surface. Install new air terminals at both ends of each screen wall, with additional terminals spaced at 20-foot intervals along the top of each wall, and at the highest point of the HVAC ductwork. Install an air terminal at each corner of the new HVAC equipment. Connect all newly installed air terminals to the existing LPS using #2 bare copper conductors. After these corrections have been completed, a qualified inspection is required to verify full compliance with NFPA 780 and UL 96A standards. Upon successful inspection, a Master Label Certificate should be issued for the lightning protection system. Contractor shall provide all equipment, materials, supplies, tools, software, supervision, and labor required for this project, which may include, but is not limited to, demolition work, providing negative pressure environment for work, and providing all new equipment, utilities, and room finishes as indicated in the plans and this SOW per VA construction standards.  The 30th Contracting Squadron (30 CONS/PKD) at Vandenberg Space Force Base (VSFB), CA, is requesting industry feedback on the dRFP for the Facility Readiness and Maintenance Execution (FRAME) contract. FRAME is the follow-on acquisition to the current Launch Operations Support Contract (LOSC) (Contract #FA4610-23-D-0001, currently performed by Call Henry, Inc.). 

 FRAME follow-on acquisition is 100% Small Business Set-Aside. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this effort is 561210 Facilities Support Services (small business size standard is $47M). 

 Description of Services, Background, and Objective: FRAME is a non-personal services contract that provides maintenance, repair, modification, and modernization for over 130 facilities, property, and equipment (P&E) supporting the nation’s space mission, defense, and test activities at VSFB and its associated geographically-separated locations. 

 The scope of work involves facility infrastructure and systems (including water and gas mains, roads, generators, power distribution, HVAC, waste systems, and roofing) alongside the execution of distinct sustainment projects and standby support for urgent repairs during select launch operations to ensure maximum operational readiness. Additionally, the contract encompasses the inspection, testing, and certification of all Space Launch Delta 30 cranes and elevators. A key change under this follow-on acquisition is that the South Vandenberg Power Plant (SVPP) is no longer a requirement and will not be carried over from the legacy LOSC to the new FRAME contract. 

 The primary objective of the FRAME contract is to ensure Real Property Installed Equipment (RPIE) and facilities are maintained and operationally ready for a variety of ballistic missile, space, guided weapon, and aircraft test and evaluation missions in support of Space Launch Delta 30 (SLD 30), 30th Civil Engineer Squadron (30 CES), 4th Launch Squadron (4 LS), 2nd Range Operations Squadron (2 ROPS), Missile Defense Agency (MDA), U. S. Space Forces - Space (S4S), 18th Space Defense Squadron (18 SDS), Sentinel, 30th Operations Support Squadron (30 OSS), 2nd Space Launch Squadron (2 SLS), the National Reconnaissance Office (NRO), and various other Range Users.

DESCRIPTION OF SERVICES. The contractor shall provide all management, tools, supplies, equipment, parts and labor necessary to maintain, repair, and inspect the real property vertical transportation equipment (VTE) at Holloman Air Force Base in a manner that will ensure continuous and safe operation (full maintenance and repair with the exception of the exclusions identified in paragraph 2.0). The VTE and their locations are listed in Appendix A.



NOTE: The term “VTE” in this PWS includes freight and passenger elevators, escalators, and may include wheelchair/stair lifts, dock levelers, and dumbwaiters.



This full maintenance contract signifies a VTE service provider (Contractor) takes total service responsibility for the equipment identified in the contract. Except those services covered in paragraph 2.0, the monthly fixed price includes all inspections, maintenance, repairs, replacements and routine & emergency service calls. This contract allows the Government to budget total yearly costs and eliminates concerns relating to individual parts repair or replacement invoicing. The Contractor assumes all responsibility and determines the amount of service visits and types of service required to keep all VTE operating safely and within the performance objectives of paragraph 6.0.

Alterations (a.k.a. modernizations) are not covered in the full maintenance service arrangement. (See Paragraph 3.2)



Acts by parties other than the Contractor of vandalism, abuse, negligence, damage resulting from rescue and recovery operations, acts of God (including damage resulting from emergency power generator power spikes and low quality) are not included in the contract.



Additional items excluded in the full maintenance coverage are cosmetic, construction, ancillary components of the VTE system including the finishing, repairing or replacement of the cab enclosure, ceiling frames, hoist way door panels, door frames, sills, car flooring, floor covering, main line power switches, main power breaker(s), hydraulic elevator jack outer



housing, buried piping, smoke and fire sensors, fire service reports, main communication feeders to controller, security systems, batteries for emergency lighting and lowering that are not solely dedicated to the VTE, air conditioners, and heaters.



Routine cleaning and refinishing of the interior of cars and the exterior of the hoist way doors and frames is not included in the basic full maintenance service.

Leased Biomedical Research Space – Jackson VA Medical Center
1. Purpose and Relationship to Needs Interview Questionnaire
This SOW is submitted concurrently with the Needs Interview Questionnaire and is
intended to supplement and clarify the functional, infrastructure, and environmental
capabilities required to renovate leased space to support VA biomedical laboratory
research activities, consistent with VA Office of Research & Development (ORD)
expectations and applicable safety requirements.
2. Project Overview
The Jackson VA Medical Center (VAMC) seeks to lease and renovate approximately 17,660
net square feet (22,958 gross square feet) of contiguous space within the surrounding
Jackson community to support an expansion of its Research Service.
The renovated facility will support:
• Six (6) laboratory teams
• Shared core equipment and support spaces
• Limited animal facilities, including:
o Short-term housing, handling, and procedure rooms
o An aquatic research room for aquatic species
The facility will be designed to support modern biomedical laboratory research, while
allowing reasonable future flexibility to accommodate changes in research scope, funding,
and personnel.

• Approximately 17,660 net square feet (22,958 GSF) of contiguous space
• Appropriate separation of laboratory, animal, aquatic, support, and office areas

modification
3.2 Environmental Controls

10/08/2026: ***Anticipated Solicitation Date, Solicitation Number as well as building description have been updated***

 08/30/2026: ***Anticipated Solicitation Date as well as building description has been updated***

 ***THE SOLICITATION NUMBER HAS BEEN UPDATED TO W912QR27RA004*** 

 DESCRIPTION: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Louisville District intends to issue a Request for Proposal (RFP ) W912QR27RA004 for the Maintenance and Repair Army Reserve (MRAR) of Area Maintenance Support Activity (AMSA) 21 at Joint Base McGuire-Dix-Lakehurst (JBMDL) in Burlington, New Jersey. The project will repair failing facility components and extend the economic life of the facility by 25 years, providing a modern maintenance facility that enables readiness for the Army Reserve units located in the surrounding area. The project scope includes the repair of the failing HVAC and electrical systems, the removal of non-structural interior walls to right-size rooms and create open flexible workspaces as required, the repair/replacement/upgrade of light fixtures with code compliant units, the installation of a code compliant fire alarm and suppression system, and the repair of electrical conduit distribution throughout the facility. The project also repairs the exterior structural elements, replaces the failing standing seam metal roof, and corrects all life safety deficiencies while maintaining the elements of the building's exterior. The restored facility will meet minimum DOD Antiterrorism standards. All hazardous materials (HAZMAT) removed as part of the demolition will be disposed of following all state and federal guidelines. 

 The Contract Duration is one thousand ninety-five (1,095) calendar days from Contract Notice to Proceed.

 TYPE OF CONTRACT AND NAICS: This RFP will be for one (1) Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) contract. The North American Industrial Classification System Code (NAICS) for this effort is 236220 - Commercial and Institutional Building Construction.

 TYPE OF SET-ASIDE: This acquisition will be a 100%Total Small Business Set-Aside. 

 

 SELECTION PROCESS: This will be a two-phase Design/Build procurement process. The proposals will be evaluated using a Best Value Tradeoff source selection process. Potential offerors are invited to submit their performance, technical, and capability information as will be described in section 00 22 16 of the Solicitation, for review and consideration by the Government. The selection process for Phase I will evaluate such factors (not necessarily in order): Past Performance and Technical Approach for Design/Build. Pro Forma Information such as bonding and financial capability will also be required to meet the minimum requirements of the solicitation

 Following completion of the evaluation of Phase I, a target of five (5) of the most highly qualified offerors will be invited to participate in Phase II. The selected offerors for Phase II will be invited to submit additional information as will be described in Section 00 22 18 of the Solicitation, for review and evaluation by the Government. The selection process for Phase II will evaluate such factors as: Design Narrative, Management Plan, and Price. Standard Form (SF) 1442 will also be required. (NOTE: The evaluation factors for Phase II are subject to change with the Phase II amendment.)

 All evaluation factors, other than cost or price, are considered approximately equal to cost or price.

 DISCUSSIONS: The Government intends to award without discussions but reserves the right to conduct discussion should it be deemed in the Government's best interest.

 

 CONSTRUCTION MAGNITUDE: The magnitude of this construction project is anticipated to be between $10,000,000 and $25,000,000.

GENERAL SPECIFICATIONS

GAOA

SCOPE OF CONTRACT



This project consists of roof and other maintenance work on the Mesa Falls Visitor’s Center on the Caribou-Targhee National Forest to provide deferred maintenance work. The facility	is operated by the Caribou-Targhee NF and Harriman State Park on the Ashton / Island Park Ranger District in Idaho Falls, Idaho.  Reroofing, painting / staining the exterior, and other minor repairs will be part of the Base Bid, and snow guards and the repair of all round framing at all overhangs will be Optional Bid Items. The existing corrugated metal panel roofing and all metal trim and flashing will be removed and replaced.  All exterior log walls, wood shingle walls, and all trim, doors, and windows will be prepped and stained / painted.  Exterior woodpecker damage will be repaired as noted.  Damaged overhang framing at one location will be repaired as noted. Work includes the removal and proper disposal of all demolished materials. Contractor shall provide all required materials. 

Detailed descriptions of bid items are included in Section 000501, Repair Office Buildings.

Demolition and Construction sequencing shall be in accordance with the drawings and specifications and as follows:

All existing flashings.  Existing flashings are not to be incorporated into new roof unless specifically called for.

Prep log walls, wood shingle walls, and all trim.

Replace sheathing as necessary

Install ice and water shield over entire roof deck.

title: NETSAFA International Training Center Support
description: The Naval Education and Training Security Assistance Field Activity (NETSAFA), Pensacola, Florida, requires educational and training services, engineering and technical services, logistics, administration, management assistance, consulting and facilitation services, and transportation support services, training liaison, special mission personnel, and curriculum development. These services may be required in various locations in the U.S. or in foreign countries and may include support to foreign governments with formal and informal schools and courses, Mobile Training Teams (MTTs), and Mobile Education Teams (METs) under the auspices of the Security Cooperation Education Training Program (SCETP)/Security Assistance Training Program (SATP). The PSC code for this action is U099 Education/Training-Other associated with NAICS code 541330 under the Knowledge Based Services Taxonomy of services. NETSAFA supports international training in all warfare areas and at all levels of training for foreign countries. This is accomplished by staffing, operating, and managing international training support provided at NETSAFAs international training sites. The training sites are located in the NETASAFA International Training Center (NITC) located at Naval Air Station (NAS) Pensacola, Florida and NAS Whiting Field, Milton, Florida, and NITC Detachment Whiting Field, Milton, Florida. These sites are outfitted with computer training facilities, classrooms, and equipment needed to teach courses. They provide training and training support services in Navy activities such as government-owned contractor operating facilities. NETSAFAs international training sites are currently operational and have established curriculum. The training and other services required by this Performance Work Statement (PWS) are currently centered in four categories: General Training Programs, Aviation Training Programs, Mobile Training Teams (MTTs), and Mobile Education Teams (METs). Additionally, support will be required to meet emerging requirements in support of the SCETP/SATP. The instant requirement is for services associated with the international requirement of the United States and the foreign countries participating in the SCETP/SATP for a 12-month base period of performance beginning 01 March 2027 through 29 February 2028, with four (4) consecutive 12-month option periods pursuant to FAR 52.217-9, and a 6-month option period pursuant to FAR 52.217-8. The contractor will be required to periodically perform these services in various locations in the U.S. and may be required to perform these services in foreign countries. If support is needed in a foreign country, the contractor may be required to support foreign governments with formal and informal schools and courses, mobile training teams, and mobile education teams under the auspices of the Security Cooperation Education Training Program (SCETP) /Security Assistance Training Program (SATP).

title: Construction of Chilled Water Plant and Site Utility Upgrades at VA Medical Center in West Haven, CT
description: The scope of the chilled water plant replacement consists of the demolition of the existing chilled water plant (building 16a) and construction of a new multi-story chilled water plant to include chillers, cooling towers, pumps, and all associated mechanical and electrical equipment. Due to the close proximity of the existing fuel tank farm adjacent to the existing chilled water plant, a new fuel tank farm will need to be constructed as part of the project, which primarily serves the central boiler plant, requiring close coordination with the medical center and ongoing related projects.The scope of the site utility upgrades consists of the replacement and upgrade of the existing fire protection water main and the domestic water main from Campbell Avenue to Building 15. Site utility upgrades also include providing utility main loops of chilled water supply and return, steam supply, condensate return, domestic water supply, and fire protection water supply which will originate from the new chilled water plant and back-feed to Building 1. The work also includes the installation of redundant electrical feeder from the utility demarcation point to Building 19 and coordination with the local electrical utility provider to provide further electrical redundancy offsite as well. In addition, new water storage tanks will be constructed. This project involves civil/site, mechanical, electrical, plumbing, structural, geotechnical, and architectural disciplines. The project must also comply with the DVAs Physical Security Resiliency Design Requirements (PSRDM). It is expected that the chilled water plant will be constructed to meet USGBC LEED Silver certification. The work is located adjacent to and within an active Medical Center campus which will be operational at all times. Impact to on-going operations must be kept to a minimum and carefully coordinated with the Contracting Officer and VAMC staff. In addition, the work area is constrained due to the active medical center operations which will limit laydown and storage areas during construction.

title: Chesapeake and Delaware (C and D) Canal Building Replacement Project.
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineer (USACE), Philadelphia District (NAP), anticipates a requirement for the Chesapeake and Delaware (C and D) Canal Building Replacement Project. The Chesapeake and Delaware or Canal connects the Delaware River to the Chesapeake Bay and Port of Baltimore. The canal is maintained from a field office located in Chesapeake City Maryland. This office consists of multiple buildings and shops that are essential to the continued operation of the canal. Several of these building have reached the end of their lifecycle and need to be replaced. This project will include the demolition and consolidation of the mechanics shop, bridge shop and storage buildings. A new building will be constructed to sever as a replacement of the buildings that are being removed. The building will be located along the east side of the project site. The building dimensions will be 60 feet x 150 feet with a clear ceiling height of 20 feet. The building will have a gable roof with the ridge running parallel to the length of the building. A pre- engineered metal building with tapered columns will be used. The columns will be enclosed with steel stud framing and gypsum board in the office areas. Vehicle and workshop areas will have propane fired heating. Office areas will be provided with air conditioning. The electrical service will be upgraded if necessary to provide power to the new building. The building will be connected into backup power from the existing diesel generator. Work will consist of the following activities: A.) The project scope includes all work required to design and construct a 9,000 square foot maintenance building in accordance with the Request for Proposal documents including the demolition of the four existing buildings and propane storage tank currently located at the site. Utilities serving each of the buildings being demolished must be demolished to the extents defined in section 02 41 00 Demolition. Requirements stated in this contract are minimums. Innovative, creative, and life cycle cost effective solutions, which meet or exceed these requirements are encouraged. Further, the Offeror is encouraged to seek solutions that will expedite construction (panelization, pre-engineered, etc.) and shorten the schedule. The intent of the Government is to emphasize the placement of funds into functional/operational requirements. Materials and methods must reflect this by choosing the most economical type of construction allowed by code for this occupancy/project. B.) The maintenance building must be provided with Heating, Ventilation, and Air Conditioning (HVAC), electrical, communications, fire protection, life safety, plumbing systems, waste oil storage, and compressed air systems. C.) A 3,000 square foot storage shed must be designed and constructed at the location identified on the site plan. The shed design must include power and lighting. D.) The scope of work also includes civil site work consisting of site paving, installation of stormwater drainage, connection into the domestic water utility, sanitary sewer utility connection for the new maintenance building, connection of existing sanitary sewer lines into the towns sanitary sewer utility, a vehicle wash area and fire hydrants. Site work is shown in Appendix A. Site electrical work must be completed to provide the maintenance building and storage shed with power fed from the existing switch gear shed. Site telecommunications work must be completed to provide the maintenance building with connection into the existing telecommunications utilities. E.) A propane storage tank must be provided onsite and be connected to the new maintenance building and the existing propane fired generator. The estimated period of performance will be 730 calendar days. The estimated magnitude of this project is between $5,000,000 and $15,000,000. 642-22-104, 36C24426R0088, Upgrade Substation Building 2, Phase 1, PHL CMCVAMC

 Proposal Due Date: 11/20/2026 at 4:00pm EST. Email proposals to Kevin Rodgers at [email]. 

 
 Corporal Michael J. Crescenz Medical Center (CMC VAMC) requires replacement of Electrical Substations 1 and 2 in order to increase electrical capacity to support future facility projects. The existing substations are approximately 29 years old and require replacement to support current and future electrical demands.

 

 This project will replace Electrical Substations 1 and 2 with new 480/277V substations each containing a 1500 kVA transformer.

 
 A temporary 480/277V substation with a 1500 kVA transformer shall be installed to maintain electrical service to the facility during demolition and construction activities. Upon completion of construction, the temporary substation shall remain installed as a spare substation for the facility. All work shall be phased to minimize service outages and maintain continuous operation of the medical center. Defined and issued bid documents (drawings and specifications) will serve as the basis of this construction project.

SECTION I: DESCRIPTION OF SERVICES
1.1 Scope of Work
The Contractor shall provide all personnel, labor, vehicles, supervision, training, tools,
Personal Protective Equipment (PPE), agricultural-grade pesticides, washdown/application
equipment, and other items necessary to perform professional biosecurity inspections,
chemical pesticide treatments, and post-treatment certification on deployable military
equipment, vehicles, and assets.
The primary objective of this contract is to safeguard the national agricultural economy,
natural resources, and native ecosystems of the United States and Partner Nations (PN)
from the introduction, establishment, and spread of invasive species, pests, and
plant/animal pathogens in accordance with Executive Order 13751 (amending Executive
Order 13112). All services must ensure that treated military materiel and gear successfully
clear United States Customs and Border Protection (CBP) and local Partner Nation
quarantine and cleanliness inspections.

shall require a complete military re-washdown and a new Contractor
inspection/treatment at the Government's expense.

title: U.S. Army Contracting Command – Detroit Arsenal (ACC-DTA) Strategic Services Branch Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO)
description:
The 2014 Quadrennial Defense Review (QDR) established innovation as a central line of effort in the national defense strategy of the United States. The decisive military advantage of the United States over its adversaries and peer competitors is steadily eroding. Consequently, under 10 United States Code (U.S.C.) § 3458 as implemented by Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS) Subpart 212.70, Contracting/Agreements Officers may acquire innovative commercial items, technologies, or services using a competitive procedure called a Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO). Under a CSO, the Department of Defense (DoD) may competitively select proposals received in response to a general solicitation, similar to a Broad Agency Announcement (BAA), based on a review of proposals by scientific, technological, or other subject-matter expert peers. Use of a CSO in accordance with DFARS Subpart 212.70 is considered to be a competitive procedure for the purposes of 10 U.S.C. Chapter 221 and Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 6.102. Finally, Contracting/Agreements Officers shall treat items, technologies, and services acquired using a CSO as commercial products and/or services. Contracts or agreements under this authority shall be fixed-price, including fixed-price incentive fee.

 The CSO is a competitive, streamlined process to obtain rapid access to solutions or new capabilities that fulfill requirements, close capability gaps, and/or provide potential technological advances. The Strategic Services Branch within the Acquisition Services Division at the Army Contracting Command – Detroit Arsenal (ACC-DTA) looks to leverage the CSO process to efficiently support a diverse range of Requirement Activities, including organizations at the Detroit Arsenal (DTA) and Selfridge Air National Guard Base (SANGB), such as the Tank-automotive and Armaments Command (TACOM), Ground Vehicle Systems Center (GVSC), Program Executive Office Ground Combat System (PEO GCS), PEO Combat Support & Combat Service Support (PEO CS&CSS), Integrated Logistics Support Center (ILSC), and the U.S. Army Garrison – Detroit Arsenal (USAG-DTA), as well as organizations located in the National Capital Region (NCR), including the Center of Military History (CMH), Center for Army Analysis (CAA), Army Museum Enterprise (AME), and National Museum of the U.S. Army (NMUSA).

 Through four specialized teams – Services Team A, Services Team B, Base Operations & Construction Team, and TACOM Service Solutions Team – the Strategic Services Branch delivers comprehensive solutions spanning information technology (IT) hardware, software, and services; museum exhibit design, fabrication, and installation services; artifact restoration and conservation services; modeling and simulation services; transcription services; custodial services; grounds and facilities services; and other support services. By streamlining acquisition and fostering collaboration with industry through this CSO, the Strategic Services Branch can procure timely, cost-effective, and innovative commercial solutions that support the mission of the many Requirement Activities we support. This agile approach is vital for adapting to evolving technological landscapes and challenges as they arise and fulfilling unique requirements across the Army; thereby, accelerating the delivery of impactful solutions, fostering a more dynamic relationship with the commercial sector, and improving operational effectiveness through the power of innovation.

 This CSO will utilize a solicitation process authorized by DFARS Subpart 212.70. Under this CSO, the DoD will be allowed to competitively procure innovative commercial items, technologies, and services. CSO procedures provide a streamlined acquisition process and simplified contract/agreement terms resulting in agreements or FAR-based contracts awarded under Part 12 Commercial Item Procedures. title: N4008527R0039 Design-Bid-Build (DBB) P-200, Aircraft Maintenance Hangar, Marine Corps Air Station (MCAS) Cherry Point, North Carolina
description:
THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS. THERE WILL NOT BE A SOLICITATION, SPECIFICATIONS, OR DRAWINGS AVAILABLE AT THIS TIME. 

 

 The Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command, Mid-Atlantic is seeking eligible small business firms capable of performing construction services for Design-Bid-Build (DBB) P-200, Aircraft Maintenance Hangar, Marine Corps Air Station (MCAS) Cherry Point, North Carolina.

 

 This project constructs all operational and support facilities to support the basing of two F-35B Lightning II squadrons at the Marine Corps Air Station (MCAS) in Cherry Point, North Carolina. New construction facilities include a low-rise, two-squadron module aircraft maintenance hangar, an aircraft parking apron, an aircraft ground/support training facility for the Center for Naval Aviation Technical Training (CNATT), a Ground Support Equipment (GSE) storage facility, an open steel-framed Operations Hazards Flammable Storage facility, and four Ready Service Magazines (RSMs). Demolition of existing facilities is required to clear the operational footprint, including the removal of Buildings 1667, 3978, 3986, 3996, 3997, 3998, 3999, and multiple hazardous waste storage shelters.

 

 The Aircraft Maintenance Hangar will be a low-rise, two-squadron module building containing high-bay space, crew and equipment space, and administrative space. The hangar will be constructed of concrete masonry units on a pile-supported reinforced concrete slab-on-grade foundation with structural steel framing, steel roof trusses, and a pre-finished insulated metal roof. Built-in equipment includes compressed air systems, personnel/freight elevators, 5-ton overhead bridge cranes, high-pressure cooling air systems, underwing and wet pipe fire suppression systems, raised access flooring, and backup generators.

 

 The Aircraft Ground/Support Training (CNATT) Facility will include administrative office spaces, five training classrooms, support spaces, and a small arms armory.

 

 The Ground Support Equipment (GSE) Storage Facility is a low-rise, high-bay single-story storage facility directly connected to the CNATT training facility.

 

 The Operations Hazards Flammable Storage Facility will be an open steel-framed structure featuring wire mesh partition separation by material type.

 

 The Ready Service Magazines (RSMs) consist of four masonry-constructed magazines (two per squadron) providing secure ammunition storage.

 

 The Aircraft Parking Apron includes new apron construction and renovation, equipped with electrical grounding, workstation kiosks, and sunshades.

description:
FA8501-27-RAPID-CIRCUIT F1-170129-OTA 

 Under the RAPID Umbrella Framework: RAPID Progressive Design-Build to Replace Circuit F-01 from Fowler Substation UHHZ170129

 Description 

 The Department of the Air Force, 78th Civil Engineer Group, Robins Air Force Base, Georgia, is issuing this Special Notice under the Robins Agile Practices for Infrastructure Development (RAPID) umbrella framework and pursuant to 10 U.S.C. § 2808a.

 The Government seeks industry Solution Briefs for an anticipated Other Transaction Agreement (OTA) to Replace Circuit F-01 from Fowler Substation at Robins AFB, GA. The requirement includes replacement of all 15kV, 500MCM cable throughout circuit F-01. This will include replacement and removal all broken breakers or bad cable racks, install new bell ends on conduits, and pump water/dirt from manholes.

 This Special Notice is not an invitation for bids, a request for proposals under the Federal Acquisition Regulation, nor a commitment by the Government to make an award. Any resulting instrument will be an OTA for facility construction and repair under 10 U.S.C. § 2808a.

 Purpose 

 The purpose of this Area of Interest is to obtain commercially viable, safe, and schedule-credible solutions to design plans for and to perform the replacement of expired high-risk Circuit F01 cabling in order to prevent operational risk, mission delays, and compounding economic costs due to infrastructure failure at Robins Air Force Base, Georgia.

 The Government requires an integrated approach to address the design, removal of deteriorated cables and replacement with new cable in The Fowler Substation. The selected approach must provide a practical path to execute the work while minimizing disruption to aircraft operations and controlling construction, safety, environmental, and schedule risks.

 Project Background and Existing Conditions 

 Circuit F-01 has surpassed its operational lifecycle, creating a high-probability risk for catastrophic failure. If the remaining aged portion is not replaced, the installation faces risk of emergency repair premiums and disruption to sustaining airfield infrastructure, supporting safe aircraft movement, installation readiness, and continued mission operations.

 The work area is slightly congested and impacted by various airfield operations. The Fowler Substation Circuit F-01 will remain in full operation during the entire duration of the project by back feeding with circuit ties.

 

 Project Areas 

 
 Phase 1 (Preconstruction & Collaborative Design): Collaborative design development stakeholders to achieve 65% , site surveys, risk mitigation planning, schedule and establishment of an open-book Guaranteed Maximum Price (GMP) IAW with all other aspects of the SOO. 

 Phase 2 (Final Design & Construction Execution) 

 

 Completion of final design and full construction execution (exercised upon agreement). Safely construct the facility/project within the agreed GMP and schedule. Assume hazardous materials exist. Address requirements for worker notification, abatement, and disposal. Employ a safety and health professional to provide a HASP per DoDI 6055.01. Comply with Robins Environmental Requirements (Section 01560) submitting Waste Management Report/Landfill Waste Tickets, Solid Waste Disposal Plan, and Qualified Recycling Program (QRP). Appropriately coordinate Stormwater & Erosion Control. Structure execution to allow for payable milestones payments, as well as all other aspects outlined in the SOO.

 
 Project-Specific Objectives and Phasing 

 

 Replace all 15kV, 500MCM cable throughout the distribution of circuit F-01 in its entirety of

multiple different installation facilities, while remaining in full operation besides outages and removing and replacing all broken breakers or bad cable racks, install new bell ends on conduits, and pump water/dirt from manholes . Address specific phasing to accommodate congested areas.

 

 OTA & RAPID Framework Approach

title: OR WARM SPRINGS QTRS 4 PAINT/FLOORING
description:
The U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service is seeking a contractor to provide all labor, materials, equipment, supervision, and incidentals necessary to perform interior painting and laminate/vinyl plank flooring installation at Warm Springs National Fish Hatchery, Warm Springs, Oregon. Work includes surface preparation, painting of designated interior quarters, removal of existing flooring, subfloor preparation, installation of new flooring, and disposal of all associated debris. 

A site visit will be held on Tuesday, November 10, at 12:00 PM PST.

Responses will assist the Government in determining the appropriate acquisition method, including whether a full or partial small business set-aside is appropriate.

 Interested small businesses may respond for Task Area A (Professional Services), Task Area B (Highly Specialized Scientific Services), or both.  Scientific & Technical Expertise Acquisition & Management (STEAM) will acquire contractor-provided services and expertise to accomplish varied project-based requirements across NIH. Contractors must furnish and manage the resources needed to perform multiple concurrent projects at substantial volume and adjust those resources as authorized project requirements change.

 NIH anticipates using cost-reimbursement contracting approximately 20 percent of the time. The actual mix will depend on individual requirements. Firms should describe their experience and ability to support this component, including any preparation needed. PRE-SOLICITATION NOTICE: The VA Illiana Health Care System (VIHCS), Danville IL, 1900 E Main St. Danville, IL 61832, has a need for a Multiple Award Task Order Contract (MATOC) for mechanical construction. The VA intends to award a MATOC for mechanical maintenance, repair, alteration, and repair of buildings and other real property belonging to this facility, with task orders ranging in value from $2,000 to $3,000,000. The VA anticipates a minimum of two (2) IDIQ contract awards and shall reserve the right to make additional IDIQ awards.
The primary purpose/work to be ordered under this contract is mechanical construction (NAICS 238220) but may include work incidental to the overall construction work, such as carpentry; asphalt and concrete paving; roofing; excavation; interior renovation; carpet, window, door installation; mechanical; electrical; plumbing; painting and stucco; demolition; masonry; fire protection; telecommunications; HVAC; and other construction-related work.

The NAICS code for this procurement is 238220 with a size standard of $19.0 Million Dollars. The construction range for the seed project is between $1,000,000 and $2,000,000.

description:
FA8501-27-RAPID-CIRCUIT F1-170129-OTA 

 Under the RAPID Umbrella Framework: RAPID Progressive Design-Build to Replace Circuit F-01 from Fowler Substation UHHZ170129

 Description 

 The Department of the Air Force, 78th Civil Engineer Group, Robins Air Force Base, Georgia, is issuing this Special Notice under the Robins Agile Practices for Infrastructure Development (RAPID) umbrella framework and pursuant to 10 U.S.C. § 2808a.

 The Government seeks industry Solution Briefs for an anticipated Other Transaction Agreement (OTA) to Replace Circuit F-01 from Fowler Substation at Robins AFB, GA. The requirement includes replacement of all 15kV, 500MCM cable throughout circuit F-01. This will include replacement and removal all broken breakers or bad cable racks, install new bell ends on conduits, and pump water/dirt from manholes.

 This Special Notice is not an invitation for bids, a request for proposals under the Federal Acquisition Regulation, nor a commitment by the Government to make an award. Any resulting instrument will be an OTA for facility construction and repair under 10 U.S.C. § 2808a.

 Purpose 

 The purpose of this Area of Interest is to obtain commercially viable, safe, and schedule-credible solutions to design plans for and to perform the replacement of expired high-risk Circuit F01 cabling in order to prevent operational risk, mission delays, and compounding economic costs due to infrastructure failure at Robins Air Force Base, Georgia.

 The Government requires an integrated approach to address the design, removal of deteriorated cables and replacement with new cable in The Fowler Substation. The selected approach must provide a practical path to execute the work while minimizing disruption to aircraft operations and controlling construction, safety, environmental, and schedule risks.

 Project Background and Existing Conditions 

 Circuit F-01 has surpassed its operational lifecycle, creating a high-probability risk for catastrophic failure. If the remaining aged portion is not replaced, the installation faces risk of emergency repair premiums and disruption to sustaining airfield infrastructure, supporting safe aircraft movement, installation readiness, and continued mission operations.

 The work area is slightly congested and impacted by various airfield operations. The Fowler Substation Circuit F-01 will remain in full operation during the entire duration of the project by back feeding with circuit ties.

 

 Project Areas 

 
 Phase 1 (Preconstruction & Collaborative Design): Collaborative design development stakeholders to achieve 65% , site surveys, risk mitigation planning, schedule and establishment of an open-book Guaranteed Maximum Price (GMP) IAW with all other aspects of the SOO. 

 Phase 2 (Final Design & Construction Execution) 

 

 Completion of final design and full construction execution (exercised upon agreement). Safely construct the facility/project within the agreed GMP and schedule. Assume hazardous materials exist. Address requirements for worker notification, abatement, and disposal. Employ a safety and health professional to provide a HASP per DoDI 6055.01. Comply with Robins Environmental Requirements (Section 01560) submitting Waste Management Report/Landfill Waste Tickets, Solid Waste Disposal Plan, and Qualified Recycling Program (QRP). Appropriately coordinate Stormwater & Erosion Control. Structure execution to allow for payable milestones payments, as well as all other aspects outlined in the SOO.

 
 Project-Specific Objectives and Phasing 

 

 Replace all 15kV, 500MCM cable throughout the distribution of circuit F-01 in its entirety of

multiple different installation facilities, while remaining in full operation besides outages and removing and replacing all broken breakers or bad cable racks, install new bell ends on conduits, and pump water/dirt from manholes . Address specific phasing to accommodate congested areas.

BASIC SERVICES
A. Organization
The Maritime Administration (MARAD)/U.S. Merchant Marine Academy (USMMA) is a federal service
academy that educates and graduates leaders of exemplary character who are inspired to serve the national
security, marine transportation, and economic needs of the United States as licensed Merchant Marine Officers
and commissioned officers in the Armed Forces.
B. Background
The Code of Federal Regulations, 46 CFR 310.62 requires Midshipmen at the USMMA to
receive limited medical and dental care. For the purposes of this statement of work (SOW),
limited medical and dental care is defined as healthcare provided using any appropriate
contractor healthcare personnel, equipment and supplies that can be reasonably made available
on site at the USMMA Department of Health Services (hereby referred to as DHS).
Referrals of Midshipmen to offsite healthcare facilities become an insurance billable event (with
exception to supportive laboratory and diagnostic work associated with onsite diagnosis and
treatment needs). Therefore, the contractor must make every reasonable attempt to provide care
for Midshipmen at DHS with the goal to eliminate off site referrals when determined clinically
safe to do so to meet the CFR 310.62 requirements and prevent unnecessary insurance billing,
co-pays and excess use of off-site facilities, such as the emergency room. The Contractor is
required to provide a quality assurance (QA) process to ensure that Midshipmen are not referred
off site for care that can be rendered on site at USMMA. As part of the request for proposals
(RFP), the contractor response should include, in addition to this QA process, a remedy for
Midshipmen who are financially impacted from having provided payment (co pays) for care that
could have been rendered on site at USMMA.
C. Scope of Work
Healthcare professionals (medical, dental, behavioral and emergency medical services) and
administrative support staff will provide limited medical and dental care services for the
Midshipmen. When determining the appropriate needs of healthcare professional staff and/or
healthcare administrative support staff the Government needs for meeting the mission of
USMMA will prevail. All medical/dental diagnostic equipment, lab services and medical/dental
recurring supplies used to examine, diagnose, render invasive or non-invasive intervention and
care of the Midshipmen at USMMA shall be supplied by the prospective contractor.
The medical/dental staff will examine, diagnose, and render invasive or non-invasive intervention and care
for an estimate of 1000 Midshipmen, male: approximately 80% and female: approximately 20%.

Information and insights gathered through this exploratory phase will directly inform the
USCG's acquisition strategy, requirements maturation, and budgeting, which will

(RFPs). Vendors are encouraged to submit responses reflecting their current commercial
offerings, operational concepts, and high-level recommendations rather than seeking
definitive contract-level specifications at this time.

Item 13 asks for instructors to oversee training, inject faults and interact with
students remotely. Item 15 asks whether the system can operate in a
completely air-gapped offline environment. Should remote instructor oversight
and fault injection remain available over an isolated government network
without internet access, or may those functions be unavailable during fully
disconnected operation? This distinction would inform separate acceptance
tests for instructor events, local student-performance logging and approved
xAPI/SCORM export.
The USCG is asking the vendor how they handle the ability to have a "classroom" stand
alone option, a remote classroom/ remote instructor (cloud based?) and the ability for a
student to sign in and take the course alone with and without guidance. The USCG is
asking industry how this might work or if they are already doing this for the military.
Tier 1 (Enterprise / Closed Intranet Mode): Remote instructor oversight, multi-student
observation, live voice interaction, and dynamic fault injection must function over an
isolated, closed Government network without requiring access to the public internet or
commercial cloud servers. Acceptance testing for distributed instructor events and remote
telemetry will evaluate performance across this closed, air-gapped network environment.
Tier 2 (Autonomous / Fully Disconnected Mode): For detached operations (e.g., deployed
cutters, isolated hangars, or network outages), individual training stations must remain
fully operable as autonomous, standalone units. In this mode, remote instructor controls
may be unavailable; however, headsets must execute all checklist, emergency, and MPC
procedures locally, record student event performance to encrypted local storage, and
queue standardized xAPI/SCORM run-time data for delayed batch synchronization once
reconnected to the enterprise environment.

title: 136 Airlift Wing C-130J Aircraft Wash
description:
The purpose of this sources sought notice is to gain knowledge of potential sources, locations, and methods. This notice is for planning purposes only. The 136th Airlift Wing, Naval Air Station Joint Reserve Base, Fort Worth, Texas, intends to issue a solicitation and award of a contract or agreement to periodically wash C-130J model aircraft. All aircraft washing and cleaning procedures shall be performed in accordance with applicable Air Force Technical Orders, including TO 1C-130J-23CL-1 and TO 1C-130J-23S-3. Contractors shall be responsible for complying with all requirements contained within the applicable Technical Orders.

 Aircraft washes are to take place at an alternate location or utilize a method that allows for outdoor wash at NASJRB Fort Worth that includes collection of run-off in accordance with installation host Navy and environmental regulations.

 All interested parties shall submit a written response to this office, not to exceed three (3) pages, addressing the following information:

 
 Company name.

 Unique Entity ID (UEI) and/or CAGE Code.

 Location where washes would occur.

 A description of access requirements for the wash location.

 A description of prior experience with washing large aircraft, highlighting any military-type washes.

 Method for completing washes.

 Indoor or outdoor washes.

 Time required on location to complete washes.

 Availability to schedule washes at the convenience of the Government.

 Confirmation that all aircraft washing and cleaning procedures will be performed in accordance with TO 1C-130J-23CL-1 and TO 1C-130J-23S-3

 Confirmation that only approved materials meeting MIL-PRF-87937 and MIL-PRF-85570 specifications will be used.

 

 NOTICE: Technical Orders 1C-130J-23CL-1 and 1C-130J-23S-3 contain distribution-restricted technical data and will not be provided as part of this Sources Sought Notice. Interested parties are not required to review these TOs for the purpose of responding to this notice.

 The requirements below identify the anticipated scope of work and key performance considerations applicable to C-130J aircraft exterior washing and corrosion control services. Any future contract award or agreement may require compliance with the current versions of applicable Technical Orders and Air Force guidance.

 Applicable Requirements for C-130J Aircraft Washes

 The contractor shall possess the capability to:

 
 Perform exterior aircraft washing of C-130J aircraft using approved aircraft cleaning methods, equipment, and materials suitable for military aircraft finishes and coatings.

 Utilize cleaning compounds, detergents, and wash procedures that are compatible with painted surfaces, transparencies, composite materials, antennas, sensors, and other aircraft components.

 Conduct freshwater rinsing procedures sufficient to remove contaminants, cleaning agents, salt deposits, dirt, oil, grease, hydraulic fluid residue, exhaust residue, and environmental pollutants.

 Prevent water intrusion into aircraft openings, vents, sensors, avionics components, pitot-static systems, and other sensitive areas during washing operations.

 Protect aircraft components and finishes from damage caused by improper washing techniques, excessive pressure, unauthorized chemicals, abrasive materials, or improper equipment use.

 Identify, document, and report visible signs of corrosion, coating deterioration, surface damage, fluid leaks, paint degradation, or other discrepancies observed during wash operations.

 Comply with all applicable Foreign Object Damage (FOD) prevention requirements while performing aircraft wash operations.

 Comply with all applicable environmental, hazardous material, hazardous waste, stormwater, and occupational safety regulations associated with aircraft washing activities.

 Provide trained and qualified personnel familiar with military aircraft washing, corrosion prevention, corrosion detection, and corrosion reporting practices.

 Furnish all labor,

STATEMENT OF WORK
FALL ARREST SYSTEM INSPECTION
Fairchild Air Force Base, Washington
DESCRIPTION OF WORK. 	Contractor shall perform annual inspections of the fall protection
systems located in building 2050 hangars No. 1, 2, 3, & 4 located at Fairchild AFB, Washington.
Building 2050 is located in a controlled area. Escorts will be provided by the government as
coordinated in advance to perform services. Non-U.S. citizen workers are prohibited from accessing
the controlled area. The annual inspection shall be performed in accordance with all federal, state,
local regulations and manufacturer recommendations. The inspection is necessary to ensure continued
compliance with OSHA Regulations and manufacturer recommendations. The contractor shall
provide an 85-foot lift to access the system.
As a minimum the inspection shall consist of the following actions:
 	A hands on inspection of all components of the installed system
 	Visually verify all end terminations
 	Tighten all lock nuts to the required torque
 	Inspect for presence of cotter pins where appropriate
 	Check for damage to all components including cable along its entire length, intermediate brackets
and end termination
 	Inspect intermediate brackets for excessive deformation

 	Inspect user equipment supplied with the original system or replacement of same make and
model, including harnesses and lanyards.
 	Perform all other actions required to comply with OSHA and/or manufacturer’s inspection
requirements.
The inspection will be limited to the engineered system components installed by Evan Corporation or
manufactured by Capital Safety Group and installed by others.

repairs that may be required.

Manager/Coordinator.

intelligence (HUMINT) gathering and consider it a HUMINT incident. Contract personnel who have

supporting Air Force Office of Special Investigations (AFOSI) office.

US Army Intelligence and Security Command (INSCOM)
Access Control Officer and Escort Support Services
Part 1
General Information
1. General: This is a non-personal services contract to provide unarmed Access Control Officers and
Escort personnel support services. The Government will not exercise any supervision or control over the
contract service providers performing the services herein. Contract service providers shall be accountable
solely to the Contractor who, in turn is responsible to the Government.
1.1 Description of Services/Introduction: The Contractor shall furnish all required labor, supervision,
uniforms, equipment, licenses, certifications, and state and local permits as non-personal services
necessary to perform the services as defined in the Performance Work Statement (PWS) except for those
items specified as government furnished property and services. This PWS provides security support
services for Access Control Officers and Escorts for the Head Quarters (HQs) INSCOM and all
subordinate commands within the United States. Services include controlling and monitoring access of
personnel and equipment for all the INSCOM Sensitive Compartmented Information Facility (SCIF) as it
relates to ensuring personnel have the required clearance and equipment/materials are marked properly.
Additionally, services include providing escort services for personnel without security clearances. The
Contractor shall perform to the standards in this single award Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity
(IDIQ).
1.1.1 Exemption to Services: In accordance with the National Capital Region statutory exception for
Access Control functions, approved new locations may be identified in individual Task Orders at no
additional cost to the Government.
1.2 Background: Headquartered at Fort Belvoir, Virginia, with 17,500 Soldiers, Department of the Army
(DA) civilians and Contractors, located at 180 locations in 45 countries, INSCOM executes mission
command of operational intelligence forces; conducts worldwide multidiscipline and all source
intelligence operations; delivers advanced skills training, linguist support, specialized quick reaction
capabilities, and intelligence-related logistics, contracting, and communications in support of Army, Joint,
and Coalition commands and the National Intelligence Community. INSCOM is a global command with
multiple major subordinate commands (MSCs). INSCOM’s units are located worldwide to provide
tailored intelligence support. All further references to INSCOM throughout this document include its
(MSCs) and other subordinate units located in the United States and abroad.
1.3 Objectives: The objective of the acquisition is to provide Access Control Officers and Escort support
services that process authorized visitors for entry, provide a deterrent to the unauthorized removal of
classified materials, prevent unauthorized entry into facilities by personnel not having a proper clearance

Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) and Army policy within the HQ INSCOM and Major Subordinate
Commands (MSC) buildings in the United States.

to HQ INSCOM and all MSCs within the United States, to include the following outlined tasks:

title: Solicitation:  Construct Combat Rescue Helicopter Flight Simulator Facility at Moffett ANGB
description:
The USPFO for California intends to award a single firm-fixed-price contract for non-personal construction services, to include all plant, labor, transportation, materials, tools, equipment, appliances, and supervision necessary for the construction of a Combat Rescue Helicopter (CRH) Operational Flight Trainer (OFT) simulator facility at Moffett Air National Guard Base (ANGB), Mountain View, California.
