sow_text:
STATEMENT OF WORK (SOW)
Milford, CT Laboratory Salt (Sea) Water Pump and Electrical Infrastructure System
Upgrade
1.0 GENERAL
1.1 BACKGROUND
The Northeast Fisheries Science Center (NEFSC) operates under the National Marine Fisheries
Service (NMFS), a part of the National Oceanographic and Atmospheric Administration
(NOAA). The agency’s core mission is the stewardship of living marine resources.
To support ongoing Milford Laboratory and the Northeast Oyster Breeding Center’s facility
resilience, process fluid infrastructure, and reliable laboratory operations, the facility requires a
complete replacement and modernization of its salt water pumping system and associated
electrical infrastructure. The existing system must be decommissioned to make way for
corrosion-resistant equipment capable of surviving a harsh coastal environment. The scope of
this requirement is directly tied to the success of the Oyster Breeding Center’s spawning cycle
and research missions. Due to the severe operational impact of any delay, the Government
requires strict adherence to the deliverables schedule.
1.2 SCOPE
The scope of this project is the complete decommissioning of existing system, and procurement,
installation, and wiring of a new corrosion-resistant salt water pumping system and its supporting
electrical distribution and plumbing infrastructure. The Contractor shall furnish all labor,
materials, equipment, transportation, and supervision required to execute the following
transitions:
● Removal of legacy disconnects, starters, wiring troughs, wiring, breakers, enclosures and
plumbing piping.
● Procurement and installation of a Vanton Chem-Gard® non-metallic horizontal
centrifugal pump assembly or equivalent.
● Installation and configuration of four (4) active WEG variable frequency drives
(VFDs/Inverters) and associated NEMA 4X enclosures or equivalent.
● Upgrading local field instrumentation, current transducers, and electrical distribution
wiring.
● Delivery of required on-site backup components (Two spare impellers, one for each
pump model) directly to facility inventory.
1.3 OBJECTIVE

-- 1 of 12 --

To safely remove legacy infrastructure and deliver an operational, highly reliable, and
corrosion-resistant salt water pumping system that offers precise local motor control for the Main
Building at the Milford Laboratory.
2.0 SPECIFIC REQUIREMENTS / TASKS
2.1 Critical Sequence of Operations (reference section 9.0 Deliverables)
Due to the severe operational impact of current seawater system, the Contractor MUST adhere to
the following mandatory sequence of execution:
● Phase 1 (Procurement): The immediate order of the WEG VFDs and Vanton Pump
assemblies to be delivered within 4 weeks of NTP.
● Phase 2 (Pre-Demolition Verification): The Contractor shall not initiate any legacy
demolition (Task 2) or shut down the existing pumps until all new VFDs, pump
assemblies, and critical electrical components are physically on-site and verified by the
COR.
● Phase 3 (Execution): Upon COR verification of materials, the Contractor may enter the
strict 10-day maximum shutdown window to execute demolition, installation, and
commissioning
2.2 TASK 1: Legacy Infrastructure Demolition
● Electrical & Pump Decommissioning: Safely isolate, apply Lock-Out/Tag-Out
(LOTO), disconnect, and completely remove all existing electrical disconnects, motor
starters, electrical wiring and plumbing associated with the legacy pump system.
● Enclosure Removal: Demolish and remove the existing legacy wire trough, old relay
enclosure, and button enclosure.
● Manual Transfer Switches: Existing manual transfer switches labeled NORMAL
POWER / EMERGENCY POWER are no longer needed and shall be removed. The
existing main power panel is on generator power, and no new manual transfer switches
are required.
● Pipe Containment: Install terminal/junction boxes on the Pumps pipes to securely
transition or isolate the existing runs as specified.
2.3 TASK 2: Pump System & Electrical Installation
2.3.1 Pump Operating & Process Fluid Parameters

-- 2 of 12 --

The procured pump assembly must be rated for continuous duty matching the following
parameters for pumps supplying Building #1:
● Fluid: Salt Water
● Specific Gravity (SG): 1.03
● Temperature: Ambient
● Flow Rate: 200,000 GPD Gallons Per Day
● Total Dynamic Head (TDH): 100 Feet
The procured pump assembly must be rated for continuous duty matching the following
parameters for pumps supplying Building #4:
● Fluid: Salt Water
● Specific Gravity (SG): 1.03
● Temperature: Ambient
● Flow Rate:350 GPM Gallons Per Minute
● Total Dynamic Head (TDH): 10 Feet
2.3.2 Pump Mechanical Specifications
The contractor shall supply and install:
● Manufacturer/Model: Two (2) 10HP Vanton Chem-Gard® ANSI horizontal centrifugal
pump, Model CGA-PY3X2X6-OP (A-10), brand name or equivalent (To supply building
#1).
● Manufacturer/Model: Two (2) 15HP (Vanton Chem-Gard® ANSI horizontal centrifugal
pump, Model CGA-KY4X3X10-OP (A-70) brand name or equivalent ( To supply
Building #4).
● Fluid Contact Parts: Homogeneous,(KYNAR) non-metallic materials.
● Shaft & Sleeve: Stainless steel shaft, wet end sleeved with PVDF (Kynar).
● Materials of Construction: Kynar (cannot be Polypropylene).
● Suction & Discharge Connections: 3" x 2" Flanged.
● Impeller: dynamically balanced keyed, semi open design.
● Shaft & Sleeve: Stainless steel shaft, wet end sleeved with PVDF (Kynar).
● Materials of Construction: Polypropylene (Kynar).
● Suction & Discharge Connections: 3" x 2" Flanged.
● Isolators: All newly installed sea water pumps shall be placed on anti-vibration pads to
minimize vibration on the existing concrete pad. There are no specific specifications on
the anti-vibration pads, any anti-vibration pads may be used.
● Plumbing: All plumbing piping shall be reconfigured to accommodate the newly
installed pumps.
● Sealing System: Double Mechanical Seal (#8 & #21).

description:
NOTICE OF INTENT TO AWARD A SOLE-SOURCE MODIFICATION 

 Security Guard Services — CDC Facilities, Metro Atlanta, Georgia and Fort Collins, Colorado 

 Contract No. 75D30125C20468

NAICS Code: 561612, Security Guards and Patrol Services (size standard: $29 Million Dollars)

Place of Performance: CDC-owned and leased facilities, metro Atlanta, Georgia and Fort Collins, Colorado

Period of the Proposed Action: January 1, 2027 through January 31, 2027

Response Date: 1:00 PM Eastern Time, November 19, 2026

 Intent and Authority 

 The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) intends to negotiate a sole-source modification to Contract No. 75D30125C20468 with Chenega Global Protection, LLC for one month of continued security guard services covering January 1 through January 31, 2027. The proposed action is authorized under FAR 6.103-1, Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements (41 U.S.C. 3304(a)(1)).

 Purpose 

 The modification will maintain continuous, uninterrupted security guard coverage at CDC facilities in metro Atlanta, Georgia and Fort Collins, Colorado during the January 2027 transition-in period of the competitively awarded follow-on contract. The ongoing requirement for these services has been competed; this action is confined to the single transition month.

 Basis for the Sole-Source Determination 

 Chenega Global Protection, LLC is the only responsible source able to perform this requirement without interruption during the January 1–31, 2027 window.

 The requirement is not merely to perform security guard services for one month. It is to assume full coverage of the security of multiple CDC campuses, including a BSL-4 select-agent laboratory and Sensitive Compartmented Information Facility (SCIF) posts on January 1, 2027 with no lapse, and to relinquish those posts to the follow-on contractor on February 1, 2027.

 Guard personnel at these posts must already hold the requisite security clearances, CDC facility credentials and access badges, site- and post-specific certifications, and current weapons qualifications. The incumbent’s workforce is already fully cleared, credentialed, badged, post-certified, and in place.

 Any source other than the incumbent would first have to complete its own transition-in — clearances, credentialing, badging, post certification, and weapons qualification — before January 1, 2027, and then immediately execute a transition-out thirty days later. The Government has determined, and has structured the follow-on contract to reflect, that a new contractor requires the full period of January 1–31, 2027 to complete transition-in alone.

 Any lapse, gap, or partial coverage would create an unacceptable risk to life safety, to the physical security of select agents at the BSL-4 laboratory, and to classified national-security information within the SCIF. Accordingly, for this limited period, only one responsible source can satisfy the agency’s requirement.

 Capability Statements 

 All responsible sources may submit a capability statement, which the agency will consider. To be responsive, a capability statement should address how the respondent would complete transition-in at the identified CDC facilities — including security clearances, credentialing, badging, post certification, and weapons qualification — so as to assume full post coverage effective January 1, 2027, and complete transition-out to the follow-on contractor by January 31, 2027, with no lapse or degradation in coverage at any point during the period.

 Notice Limitations 

 This notice is not a request for competitive quotations and is not a solicitation. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed action based on responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive

title: ISBEE Solicitation: Emergency Department Registered Nurse Services (Up to 8 RNs) – Standing Rock Service Unit, Fort Yates IHS Hospital, Fort Yates, ND.
department: HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES, DEPARTMENT OF
description:
The Indian Health Service (IHS), Great Plains Area, is soliciting proposals for non-personal Emergency Department Registered Nurse services in support of the Standing Rock Service Unit, Fort Yates Hospital, Fort Yates, North Dakota, under Solicitation No. 75H70627R00002.

 The requirement is for up to eight (8) qualified Emergency Department Registered Nurse positions to support continuous 24-hour, 7-day-per-week Emergency Department operations. The anticipated contract type is Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP), commercial services, with one four (4)-month Base Period and fourteen (14) four-month Option Periods, for a total potential period of performance of sixty (60) months.

 This acquisition is set aside 100 percent for eligible Indian Small Business Economic Enterprises (ISBEEs) in accordance with the Buy Indian Act and applicable HHSAR requirements. The applicable NAICS code is 561320, Temporary Help Services, and the Product Service Code is Q401, Medical–Nursing.

 The Contractor will be responsible for providing qualified nursing personnel and all associated management, supervision, recruitment, credentialing, scheduling, replacement staffing, administrative support, and other resources necessary to perform the requirements of the Performance Work Statement.

 The requirement consists of up to eight (8) separately exercisable RN positions. The Base Period provides for up to eight (8) RN position CLINs, with the actual number of Base Period RN position CLINs awarded or funded identified in the resulting contract. During each Option Period, the Government may independently exercise from one (1) up to eight (8) RN position CLINs based on operational requirements and availability of funds. The Government is not obligated to award, fund, or exercise all eight RN positions, any particular RN position, or any Option Period.

 Pricing will be based on a common Firm-Fixed-Price RN Month of Service (RN/MOS) unit price for each performance period. The common RN/MOS unit price will apply uniformly to all RN positions within that performance period. The Total Evaluated Price will be based on the maximum potential requirement for the Base Period and all fourteen Option Periods; evaluation of all RN position CLINs and option prices does not obligate the Government to award, fund, or exercise all positions or options.

 Important Dates: Questions regarding the solicitation are due no later than November 13, 2026, at 12:00 p.m. Central Time. Proposals are due no later than November 30, 2026, at 12:00 p.m. Central Time.

 Award will be made using a Best Value Tradeoff process. Evaluation factors are Past Performance, Technical Approach, Management Approach, and Price. Past Performance, Technical Approach, and Management Approach, when combined, are more important than Price. Technical Approach and Management Approach will be evaluated using adjectival ratings of Outstanding, Good, Acceptable, Marginal, or Unacceptable. The Government may select a higher-priced proposal when the evaluated benefits of the non-price factors justify the associated price premium.

 Offerors are responsible for reviewing the complete solicitation package, including the Performance Work Statement, Price Schedule/Bid Sheet, applicable FAR/HHSAR provisions and clauses, Buy Indian Act/ISBEE representations, wage determination, and any amendments, prior to submitting an offer.

1.0 GENERAL

This Performance Work Statement (PWS) describes the requirements for non-personal healthcare services to provide Emergency Department nursing services in support of the Indian Health Service (IHS), Standing Rock Service Unit (SRSU), Fort Yates Hospital (FYH).

The Contractor shall provide all management, supervision, labor, personnel, credentialing, scheduling, administrative support, and other resources necessary to perform the requirements identified in this PWS, except for those items specifically identified as Government Furnished Information, Property, or Services.

The Contractor shall maintain responsibility for the supervision, management, scheduling, and control of Contractor personnel performing under this contract. Contractor personnel shall not be considered employees of the Federal Government and shall not be subject to Government supervision or control normally exercised over Federal employees.

The Contractor shall perform all services in accordance with applicable Federal, State, and local laws and regulations; Indian Health Service policies and procedures; healthcare accreditation standards; and the terms and conditions of the resulting contract.

The Contractor shall provide qualified Emergency Department nursing personnel necessary to ensure continuous Emergency Department operations at Fort Yates Hospital, twenty-four (24) hours per day, seven (7) days per week, including holidays.

The Contractor shall be responsible for recruitment, credentialing, privileging, scheduling, supervision, replacement personnel, and overall management of Contractor employees necessary to fulfill the requirements of this contract.



1.1 BACKGROUND

The Indian Health Service (IHS) is an agency within the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) responsible for providing Federal healthcare services to American Indians and Alaska Natives.

The provision of healthcare services to members of federally recognized Tribes is based upon the special government-to-government relationship between the Federal Government and Indian Tribes.

IHS is the principal Federal healthcare provider and health advocate for American Indians and Alaska Natives. The mission of IHS is to raise the physical, mental, social, and spiritual health of American Indians and Alaska Natives to the highest level.

The Standing Rock Service Unit (SRSU), located within the Great Plains Area Indian Health Service, provides healthcare services to eligible American Indian and Alaska Native beneficiaries.

The Fort Yates Hospital (FYH) is a rural critical access hospital and Level IV Trauma Center located in Fort Yates, North Dakota. The facility provides emergency medical services requiring continuous nursing support to ensure safe, effective, and timely patient care.

Due to ongoing healthcare workforce shortages and recruitment challenges, the Government requires contracted Emergency Department nursing services to maintain continuity of healthcare operations.



1.2 SCOPE

The Contractor shall provide professional Emergency Department nursing services to support the healthcare mission of the Standing Rock Service Unit.

The Contractor shall provide qualified registered nursing personnel necessary to support emergency patient care, including patient assessment, treatment support, monitoring, documentation, care coordination, and other nursing services within the scope of practice.

The Contractor shall provide sufficient qualified personnel to maintain continuous Emergency Department coverage throughout the period of performance.

The Contractor shall provide complete nursing services as described herein. The Government is purchasing the required nursing service capability and availability and is not purchasing individual labor hours.

The Contractor shall maintain responsibility for staffing, scheduling, supervision, and management of Contractor personnel while ensuring compliance with all requirements of this PWS.



1.2.1 Duties and Responsibilities

The Contractor shall provide Emergency Department nursing services in accordance with Section 5.0, Performance Requirements.

Contractor nursing personnel shall perform duties consistent with the requirements of a rural critical access hospital Emergency Department and shall support inpatient nursing services when necessary to ensure continuity of patient care.

The Contractor shall ensure all personnel performing services under this contract possess the required qualifications, licenses, certifications, experience, and credentials identified in Section 6.0.



1.2.2 Place of Performance

The primary place of performance shall be:

Standing Rock Service UnitFort Yates Hospital10 Standing Rock AvenueFort Yates, ND 58538

The Contractor may be required to perform services within other designated areas of the facility when necessary to support patient care operations.



1.2.3 Period of Performance

The period of performance shall consist of a four (4)-month Base Period plus fourteen (14) four-month Option Periods, for a total potential period of sixty (60) months (five years).

The anticipated start of performance is approximately forty-five (45) calendar days after contract award.

The actual dates for the Base Period and each Option Period will be established in the resulting contract.

The Government reserves the right to exercise Option Period RN CLINs in accordance with the terms and conditions of the resulting contract.



1.2.4 Base Period and Option Period Structure
